details:
REFUTED. db spans do work on bun 1.4.0 with Astro 7.3.1 + @astrojs/node standalone + @sentry/astro 10.67.0 (develop), on both trace lifecycles and on both mysql2 code paths, after adding four lines to `sentry.server.config.mjs`. The other agent's two diagnoses (an "injected wrapper reads its own hasSubscribers=false" mystery and a "waitForTracingChannelBinding 1ms race") are both symptoms of one Bun runtime bug that I isolated to a 12-line script. ROOT CAUSE (Bun, not the SDK, not Astro): Bun's `node:diagnostics_channel` registry does not keep a channel alive once it has subscribers. Node's registry does (its WeakReference map is incRef'd when a channel becomes active). On Bun, as soon as the *creator* of the handle drops it, the channel is collected and every subscriber is silently dropped; the next `tracingChannel(name)` call, from mysql2's `lib/tracing.js` or from the orchestrion-injected wrapper, gets a brand-new object with no subscribers. That is exactly why Sentry reads `hasSubscribers = true` and the wrapper reads `false`: two different channel objects for the same name. Minimal repro, $S/deep/verify4-M-astro-bun-dbspans/weak1.mjs (A drops the handle, B keeps it on globalThis): == bun 1.4.0 == == node v26.5.0 == sync A: true B: true sync A: true B: true afterGC A: false B: true afterGC A: true B: true +200ms A: false B: true +200ms A: true B: true B fired A fired / B fired This also explains toolbox finding K11 ("a driver whose instrumented module first loads inside a request gets no spans on Bun") — under Astro the db page chunk loads on the first request, long after `Sentry.init()` in the preload, so a GC has always run in between. The 1ms `waitForTracingChannelBinding` retry is a red herring: my run showed `mysql2:query start.hasSubscribers` = true synchronously after init on bun and false at +0ms, i.e. Sentry does subscribe, then loses it. BASELINE (reproduces the report), `bun --preload ./sentry.server.config.mjs dist/server/entry.mjs`, traceLifecycle static, sink 53117 — 4 db routes, all empty: transaction | GET /db2 | [] transaction | GET /pool2 | [] transaction | GET /db1 | [] transaction | GET /pool1 | [] event | sentinel FIXED, same build, same bun, only the pin added (traceLifecycle static): transaction | GET /db2 | ['db mysql2.connect', 'db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?'] transaction | GET /pool2 | ['db mysql2.pool.connect', 'db mysql2.connect', 'db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?'] transaction | GET /db1 | ['db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 1'] transaction | GET /pool1 | ['db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 1'] FIXED with traceLifecycle 'stream' (the develop default), same pin: span | ['db mysql2.connect', 'db SELECT users', 'http.server GET /db2'] span | ['db mysql2.pool.connect', 'db mysql2.connect', 'db SELECT users', 'http.server GET /pool2'] span | ['db SELECT users', 'http.server GET /db1'] span | ['db SELECT users', 'http.server GET /pool1'] Both mysql2 ranges are covered by the one fix: /db2 and /pool2 use mysql2 3.24.3's native `mysql2:query|execute|connect|pool:connect` channels; /db1 and /pool1 use mysql@2.18.1 through the Astro integration's build-time `orchestrion:mysql:query` injection. So the orchestrion path the report tested with mysql2 3.19.1 is not separately broken — the same pin revives it. Variants tried: - Pin as a separate preload before init (`pinboot.mjs`) — works. - Pin inside `sentry.server.config.mjs` after `Sentry.init()` (`sentry.server.config.pin3.mjs`) — works, and this is the form I recommend (same file the Astro integration already injects, no extra preload entry needed beyond the `--preload` the app needs anyway). - Generic form, patching `tracingChannel`/`channel` on the CJS module object via `createRequire` to retain every channel ever created (`pinall2.mjs`) — works and needs no channel-name list; this is the shape an SDK-side fix would take. Patching the ESM namespace object instead throws `TypeError: Attempted to assign to readonly property` on bun, so `createRequire` is required for the generic form. - Importing the drivers before init (`dbboot.mjs`: `import 'mysql2'; import 'mysql'`) — PARTIAL: fixes mysql2 (its own module-scope consts then own the channels) but not mysql@2, whose channels exist only in the Astro-bundled, orchestrion-transformed copy. So "load your driver early" is not a sufficient instruction. - Node control with the same pin — unchanged, all db spans present. The pin is harmless on Node, so it can be applied unconditionally. - No `--preload` at all is still required to be avoided (the integration only inlines init into `.astro` page chunks); that is the other agent's separate finding and I did not re-derive it. - bun 1.3.14 (CI pin): not-run, `$S/bun1314` no longer exists on this machine. SDK-side fix location: `packages/server-utils/src/tracing-channel.ts` `bindTracingChannelToSpan()` receives the `TracingChannel` object and subscribes to it but keeps no reference; pushing the channel into a module-level array there (or in `packages/core/src/asyncContext/tracing-channel-binding.ts`'s callers) would make every channel-based integration — mysql2, mysql, redis, knex, graphql, mongoose, vercel-ai, postgres, the AI providers — survive GC on Bun. The repo's own reference app `dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/astro-7` runs `node ./dist/server/entry.mjs` and never exercises bun, which is why this is uncovered. Files (rerunnable): $S/deep/verify4-M-astro-bun-dbspans/ — `weak1.mjs` (runtime bug in isolation), `astro.config.mjs`, `sentry.server.config.mjs` (baseline), `sentry.server.config.pin3.mjs` (fix), `pinboot.mjs`, `pinall2.mjs`, `dbboot.mjs`, `src/pages/{db1.astro,db2.astro,pool1.ts,pool2.ts,sentinel.ts}`, `src/db-lib.ts`, logs `runA.log` (baseline) through `runG.log` (node control), `dist/` kept. `node_modules` removed; reinstall with `npm install $S/pack/sentry-{astro,browser,browser-utils,bundler-plugins,core,feedback,node,opentelemetry,replay,replay-canvas,server-runtime-injection,server-utils}-10.67.0.tgz astro@^7.3.1 @astrojs/node@^11.1.5 mysql2 mysql`, then `npx astro build`. Run: `PORT=

HOST=127.0.0.1 SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:/ bun --preload ./sentry.server.config.pin3.mjs dist/server/entry.mjs`.
docsImpact: On Bun, `node:diagnostics_channel` does not keep a channel alive once it has subscribers, so Sentry's database, cache and AI instrumentation stops recording spans as soon as a garbage collection runs between `Sentry.init()` and the first query — keep the channels reachable by adding `globalThis.__sentryPinnedChannels ??= ['mysql2:query','mysql2:execute','mysql2:connect','mysql2:pool:connect','orchestrion:mysql:query','orchestrion:mysql2:query','orchestrion:mysql2:execute'].map(name => require('node:diagnostics_channel').tracingChannel(name));` to your `sentry.server.config.mjs`, and start the Astro Node build with `bun --preload ./sentry.server.config.mjs dist/server/entry.mjs`.

details:
Confirmed broken as reported, and I found the root cause plus a fully working user-side fix (see workaround), so nothing in the documented Astro/Deno wiring refutes it.

Probe: $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-astro-deno-outgoingfetch/ (Astro 7.3.1 output:'server' + @deno/astro-adapter 0.6.0 + @sentry/astro 10.67.0 develop, deno 2.9.0, built dist/server/entry.mjs). Full recipe in RERUN.md; logs app-v2-base.log / app-v2-cf.log / app-v2-custom-stream.log.

Commands:
  npm install --no-audit --no-fund
  PORT=53821 node sink.mjs &   PORT=53822 node rec.mjs &
  SINK_PORT=53821 REC_PORT=53822 LIFECYCLE=static [FETCH_FIX=cloudflare|custom] \
    deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-run dist/server/entry.mjs
  curl :53823/ ; curl :53823/outfetch ; curl :53823/outhttp ; curl :53823/sentinel
  curl :53821/__items ; curl :53822/__hits

1) BASELINE, stock wiring, traceLifecycle 'static' (broken, matches the report verbatim):
{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /outfetch","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"672c185045bb409393cc084fc369f106","sdk":"sentry.javascript.astro","spans":[]}
{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /outhttp","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"e6005df74f8642a2a2aaa5c4b2fa4830","sdk":"sentry.javascript.astro","spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:53822/rec"]}
recorder hits:
  {"url":"/rec?via=fetch","sentryTrace":null,"baggage":null}
  {"url":"/rec?via=http","sentryTrace":"e6005df74f8642a2a2aaa5c4b2fa4830-92b4788a85970d32-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,...,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fouthttp,sentry-sampled=true,..."}

2) Things that do NOT change it: the other trace lifecycle (stream produces the same fetch-less span envelope), the documented Astro integration wiring, sourcemaps on/off, the src/middleware.ts init placement, node:http on the same process (always works). No bundler or Deno flag variant matters because the failure is below the SDK.

3) ROOT CAUSE (dc-probe.mjs, run under deno 2.9.0):
  after global fetch, channels fired: []
  after node:http get, channels fired: ["http.client.request.created","http.client.request.start","http.client.response.finish"]
Deno's global fetch publishes no node:diagnostics_channel events at all (neither "undici:request:*" nor "http.client.*"). @sentry/node's only outgoing-fetch path is the vendored undici diagnostics_channel instrumentation (packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/undici-instrumentation.ts, shipped as nativeNodeFetchIntegration), so it can never observe Deno's fetch. Export check on the installed builds: @sentry/node and @sentry/astro expose only `nativeNodeFetchIntegration`; a globalThis.fetch-patching `fetchIntegration` exists only in @sentry/bun (packages/bun/src/integrations/fetch.ts) and @sentry/cloudflare (packages/cloudflare/src/integrations/fetch.ts), plus `winterCGFetchIntegration` in @sentry/vercel-edge. @sentry/deno ships none. That asymmetry, not Astro, is the gap.

4) The repo's own e2e app agrees: ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/deno/tests/fetch.test.ts asserts only the hand-written `Sentry.startSpan({name:'test-outgoing-fetch'})` wrapper (`origin: 'manual'`) and never an `http.client` span, so the Deno suite does not cover automatic fetch instrumentation. astro-7 (the Astro reference app) runs on @astrojs/node, not Deno, so it never exercises this.

5) With a fetch integration added, the capability works completely (both lifecycles), which proves the runtime can support it and the only missing piece is SDK-shipped code:
  FETCH_FIX=cloudflare, static:
  {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /outfetch","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"87e311391b7b4e73bcd852eaeb4155d6","spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:53822/rec"]}
  {"url":"/rec?via=fetch","sentryTrace":"87e311391b7b4e73bcd852eaeb4155d6-9948eb2f76ac150b-1","baggage":"...sentry-trace_id=87e311391b7b4e73bcd852eaeb4155d6,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Foutfetch,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rate=1"}
  FETCH_FIX=custom, stream:
  {"type":"span","trace_id":"a26095c579e649eeb43ecb3e73d1507e","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","http.server GET /outfetch"],"raw":[{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"a5a58ddf030a4cf2","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.http.fetch"},{"name":"GET /outfetch","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.astro"}]}
  {"url":"/rec?via=fetch","sentryTrace":"a26095c579e649eeb43ecb3e73d1507e-b98ee9403a04bf8b-1","baggage":"...sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Foutfetch,sentry-sampled=true,..."}

Side note reconfirmed: without src/middleware.ts importing sentry.server.config.js first, Sentry.init never runs for requests that only hit .ts/.js endpoint routes; the .astro page injection path is what warms it otherwise.
docsImpact: On Deno, `@sentry/node` (and therefore `@sentry/astro`, `@sentry/nuxt`, `@sentry/sveltekit` and every other Node-based framework SDK running on a Deno adapter) cannot instrument the global `fetch()`, because Deno's `fetch` emits none of the `node:diagnostics_channel` events the SDK's `nativeNodeFetchIntegration` subscribes to: outgoing `fetch` calls get no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, so the trace stops at your server; use `node:http`/`node:https` instead, or add a `globalThis.fetch`-patching integration built on `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest` from `@sentry/core` (the same one `@sentry/bun` and `@sentry/cloudflare` ship as `fetchIntegration`), which restores both the span and the propagation headers. The same page must also state that on a Deno adapter you need a `src/middleware.ts` whose first line is `import '../sentry.server.config.js';`, otherwise `Sentry.init` never runs for requests that only hit `.ts`/`.js` endpoint routes.

details:
Could not refute. Reproduced the reported split exactly, in both trace lifecycles, and every refutation attempt failed.

Probe dir: $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-elysia-bun-dbspans (app.ts, instrument.ts, build.ts, preload.ts, run1..run5 logs, raw-run3.json). node_modules removed after the run; recreate with:
npm install elysia@1.4 mysql2 mysql@2.18.1 $S/pack/sentry-{elysia,bun,node,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry}-10.67.0.tgz
Sink: PORT=47231 node $S/qs/sink.mjs. App is one Elysia app, Sentry.withElysia(new Elysia()), module-scope mysql2 pool AND module-scope mysql@2 connection, routes /m2/:id and /m1/:id, MariaDB 127.0.0.1:3307.

Run 1 — `SINK_PORT=47231 APP_PORT=41903 LIFECYCLE=static bun app.ts` (no bundler, documented wiring, instrument.ts imported first):
  GET /m2/:id | http.server | spans: ['middleware Request', ..., 'handler Handle', 'db mysql2.pool.connect', 'db mysql2.connect', 'db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ?', ...]
  GET /m1/:id | http.server | spans: ['middleware Request', ..., 'handler Handle', 'middleware AfterHandle', ...]   <- no db span
mysql2 works with no plugin; mysql@2 produces nothing. Confirms the report.

Run 2 (refutation attempt: runtime plugin instead of a bundle) — preload.ts sets globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__ = { bundler: new Set() } and calls Bun.plugin(sentryBunPlugin()), then `bun --preload ./preload.ts app.ts`. The process dies at import:
  SyntaxError: Missing 'default' export in module '.../node_modules/mysql2/promise.js'
  Bun v1.4.0 (macOS arm64)
So the runtime hook not only fails to add mysql@2 spans, it breaks the driver that worked. This is intentional: packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/bundler/bun.ts says "This is BUILD-ONLY. Runtime instrumentation (`bun run`) is intentionally not offered: a module returned by a runtime `onLoad` plugin in Bun loses its CommonJS named exports" (blocked on oven-sh/bun#31770). PluginOptions (bundler/options.ts) has no way to narrow the transform to one package, so a selective runtime plugin is not reachable through the public API either.

Run 3 — `bun build.ts` (Bun.build, entrypoints ['./app.ts'], target 'bun', sourcemap 'external', plugins [sentryBunPlugin()], NO `external` at all) then `LIFECYCLE=static bun dist/app.js`: both drivers produce db spans and Elysia routing is unchanged:
  GET /m1/:id | http.server | spans: [... 'handler Handle', 'db SELECT id, name FROM users', ...]
  GET /m2/:id | http.server | spans: [... 'db mysql2.pool.connect', 'db mysql2.connect', 'db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ?', ...]
Attributes on the bundled mysql@2 span are complete: sentry.origin auto.db.mysql, db.system.name mysql, db.namespace app, db.user root, db.query.text "SELECT id, name FROM users", db.query.summary "SELECT users", server.address 127.0.0.1, server.port 3307.

Run 4 — same bundle, LIFECYCLE=stream: both drivers land in the request trace with low-cardinality names:
  8a0b130b | db SELECT users | parent= 8bdb1e18 | origin= auto.db.mysql        (mysql@2, /m1)
  82245f5d | db SELECT users | parent= 9df9c06c | origin= auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel (/m2)
  8a0b130b | http.server GET /m1/:id | parent= - | origin= auto.http.elysia

Run 5 — plain `bun app.ts` with debug: true. The SDK gives no actionable warning; it logs
  Sentry Logger [warn]: No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping.
  Sentry Logger [log]: [instrumentation:mysql] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly
  Sentry Logger [log]: Integration installed: Mysql
i.e. it reports the mysql integration as installed while no channel will ever publish. Without debug there is no output at all, so the silent gap is invisible.

Two secondary observations: (a) db spans parent to the http.server root span, not to the `handler` span, in both drivers and both lifecycles; (b) mysql2 emits two extra connection spans (`mysql2.pool.connect`, `mysql2.connect`) on the first request through a pool.

Reference: the repo's own e2e apps agree — dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/bun-mysql uses build.ts with sentryBunPlugin() for mysql@2, while elysia-bun runs `bun src/app.ts` with no bundler and has no db test.
workaround: Either use `mysql2` (it publishes node:diagnostics_channel itself, so db spans work under plain `bun app.ts` with no build step), or, for any driver that does not — `mysql`@2 among them — add a build step: build.ts with `Bun.build({ entrypoints:['./app.ts'], outdir:'./dist', target:'bun', sourcemap:'external', plugins:[sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin`, then run `bun dist/app.js`. Do not pass any `external` (and never `packages:'external'` or `'*'`), and do not try `Bun.plugin(sentryBunPlugin())` in a `--preload` file: it is build-only and crashes the app at import.
docsImpact: On Bun, `@sentry/elysia` instruments only libraries that publish `node:diagnostics_channel` events themselves (e.g. `mysql2`); for every other library — `mysql`, Express, Koa, Fastify, Hapi, AI SDKs — you must bundle your app with `Bun.build({ ..., plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` and run the bundle (`bun dist/app.js`), because there is no runtime instrumentation hook on Bun; without that build step the spans are silently missing, and registering the plugin via `Bun.plugin()` in a `--preload` file is not supported and will break CommonJS imports.

details:
Reproduced exactly, and could not refute it with any wiring. @sentry/elysia 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on bun 1.4.0, elysia 1.4.

Probe dir: $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-elysia-bun-sdkname/ (RERUN.sh has every command; node_modules removed after the run, RERUN.sh reinstalls it).

Wirings tried, all with `Sentry.withElysia(new Elysia())` wrapping the fresh instance before routes, `bun app.ts`, no --preload, no bundler:

A) separate instrument.ts imported as the first line of app.ts, traceLifecycle 'stream' (default)  -> BROKEN
B) init inline at the top of the entry file, traceLifecycle 'static'                                -> BROKEN
The repo's own e2e app (~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/elysia-bun/src/app.ts) uses exactly shape B (inline init, traceLifecycle 'static'), so the reference app is affected too. `grep -rn "sentry.javascript.elysia"` over packages/ and dev-packages/ returns zero hits: nothing in the repo asserts the SDK name, which is why this ships unnoticed.

A) sink, stream lifecycle, GET /users/42 + /boom + sentinel:
  CLIENT_SDK_METADATA={"sdk":{"name":"sentry.javascript.bun","packages":[{"name":"npm:@sentry/bun","version":"10.67.0"}],"version":"10.67.0"}}
  event | env=sentry.javascript.bun@10.67.0 | pkgs=npm:@sentry/bun | elysia-boom
  event | env=sentry.javascript.bun@10.67.0 | pkgs=npm:@sentry/bun | sentinel
  span  | env=sentry.javascript.bun@10.67.0 | ... sentryOnRequest | Request | ... | GET /users/:id

B) sink, static lifecycle, inline init:
  CLIENT_SDK_METADATA={"sdk":{"name":"sentry.javascript.bun","packages":[{"name":"npm:@sentry/bun","version":"10.67.0"}],"version":"10.67.0"}}
  transaction | env=sentry.javascript.bun@10.67.0 | pkgs=npm:@sentry/bun | GET /users/:id (http.server)
  event       | env=sentry.javascript.bun@10.67.0 | pkgs=npm:@sentry/bun | elysia-boom

The `CLIENT_SDK_METADATA` line is `Sentry.getClient().getOptions()._metadata` read in the app itself, so this is settled inside `init`, before any transport or event processor, and no init placement, entry shape, lifecycle, or bundler variant can move it.

Root cause confirmed at source, exactly as reported. packages/elysia/src/sdk.ts:

  export function init(userOptions: ElysiaOptions = {}): NodeClient | undefined {
    const options = { ...userOptions, platform: 'javascript', runtime: getRuntime(), serverName: ... };
    applySdkMetadata(userOptions, 'elysia', ['elysia', options.runtime.name]);
    ...
    return initNode(options);
  }

`applySdkMetadata` (packages/core/src/utils/sdkMetadata.ts) does `(options._metadata = options._metadata || {}).sdk = ...`. When the caller passes no `_metadata`, the spread has already produced an `options` object with no `_metadata` key, so `applySdkMetadata` creates a brand-new object on `userOptions` that `options` never sees. `options` then reaches `@sentry/bun`'s `_init`, which does `applySdkMetadata(userOptions, 'bun')` correctly (packages/bun/src/sdk.ts:143 — before its own spread) and stamps `sentry.javascript.bun`.

Sibling packages get the ordering right, which shows this is a plain slip and not a design choice: packages/hono/src/bun/sdk.ts:25, node/sdk.ts:20, deno/sdk.ts:25 all call `applySdkMetadata(options, 'hono', [...])` on the already-copied object.

One-line SDK fix, proven: patch `applySdkMetadata(userOptions, "elysia"` -> `applySdkMetadata(options, "elysia"` in node_modules/@sentry/elysia/build/{esm,cjs}/sdk.js, rerun wiring A unchanged:
  CLIENT_SDK_METADATA={"sdk":{"name":"sentry.javascript.elysia","packages":[{"name":"npm:@sentry/elysia","version":"10.67.0"},{"name":"npm:@sentry/bun","version":"10.67.0"}],"version":"10.67.0"}}
  event | env=sentry.javascript.elysia@10.67.0 | pkgs=npm:@sentry/elysia,npm:@sentry/bun | elysia-boom
  span  | env=sentry.javascript.elysia@10.67.0 | ... GET /users/:id
Both the envelope header and the event payload then carry `sentry.javascript.elysia` with both packages listed, on stream and static lifecycle alike.

Same `init` is used by the elysia-node entry, so @sentry/elysia on node is affected identically (not separately run here).
docsImpact: The elysia guide's front matter already declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.elysia` (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/index.mdx:4), but the shipped package reports `sentry.javascript.bun` on every event, transaction and span, so until the SDK is fixed the page needs a note under the install/configure step: "Known issue: events sent by `@sentry/elysia` are currently tagged with `sdk.name: sentry.javascript.bun` instead of `sentry.javascript.elysia`. This only affects the SDK name shown on the event and any filtering or quota rules keyed on it; instrumentation, spans and error capture are unaffected." No docs-side wiring change helps, so the page must not suggest a different init placement, entry shape, or trace lifecycle as a remedy.

details:
The exact change that fixes it: build the Worker with Vite + `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` instead of letting `wrangler dev` bundle `src/index.ts` with its own esbuild. Nothing in the app code had to change. The plugin's `buildTimeInstrumentation` (default true) injects `diagnostics_channel.tracingChannel` calls into the bundled `mysql2` and registers the Sentry subscriber factory; plain wrangler/esbuild does not, which is why the original probe saw `spans: []`.

Requiring the Vite plugin is therefore the documented, recommended path (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx:18 "We recommend building your Cloudflare Worker with Vite and the sentryCloudflareVitePlugin plugin. Refutation attempts that did NOT open an alternative path (all recorded, none change the verdict):
- Non-Vite bundling: `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` exists and DOES inject (`orchestrion:mysql2:query` / `orchestrion:mysql2:execute` present in dist-esbuild*/index.js), but a hand-rolled esbuild pre-bundle does not boot on workerd — `Uncaught Error: Dynamic require of "tty" is not supported`, then after node:-prefixing and a createRequire banner `Uncaught Error: No such module "node:process"` — because pre-bundling bypasses wrangler's/@cloudflare/vite-plugin's unenv node-compat aliasing. `@sentry/cloudflare` exports only ".", "./request" and "./vite", so there is no supported non-Vite path.
- `vite dev` (which the docs offer as the replacement for `wrangler dev`) cannot start this app at all: `TypeError: The "superCtor.prototype" property must be of type object. Received undefined` in @cloudflare/vite-plugin's runner-worker. This is NOT Sentry's fault — the identical failure occurs with `cloudflare()` alone (vite.config.nosentry.mjs, wDevNS.log). Use `vite build` + `wrangler dev` for express-on-workerd.

One real caveat, and it is an express defect rather than a db defect: with `buildTimeInstrumentation` on (the default), registering routes at module scope crashes the Worker at startup —
  ✘ [ERROR] service core:user:v4_express_db_b: Uncaught Error: Disallowed operation called within global scope. Asynchronous I/O (ex: fetch() or connect()), setting a timeout, and generating random values are not allowed within global scope.
      at null.<anonymous> (index.js:58643:37) in route2
Line 58643 of distb/v4_express_db_b/index.js is `return tr_ch_apm$register.start.runStores(__apm$ctx, () => {`, i.e. the injected `orchestrion:router:register` channel already has subscribers at module-evaluation time (the injected snippet runs `globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION_INJECT__ = orchestrionModuleInjected("router", expressIntegration)` when `router` is first required) and the subscriber does work workerd forbids in global scope. Control proves Sentry causes it: the same src2/index.js built with `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ buildTimeInstrumentation: false })` (vite.config.c.mjs, distc) boots and serves `/db` fine. Module-scope `import mysql from 'mysql2/promise'` is not affected — only calling an instrumented express API at module scope is. Creating the mysql connection inside the request handler is fine on workerd and still produces both db spans.

Also confirmed: mysql2 needs `disableEval: true` in the connection options; without it the query text generation throws `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context` (the connect and query spans are still emitted). The `mysql@2` driver needs no such flag.

workaround: Build the Worker with Vite: `vite.config.mjs` = `defineConfig({ plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()] })`, then `npx vite build && npx wrangler dev --config dist/<worker>/wrangler.json` (not plain `wrangler dev`, and not `vite dev` — that shape cannot start express on workerd at all). Because the injected express channel makes a module-scope `app.get(...)` crash the Worker in global scope, build the express app lazily on the first request: keep `const inner = httpServerHandler({ port: 8080 })` at module scope but create the app and call `app.listen` inside `fetch` (`let listening; async fetch(req, env, ctx) { if (!listening) { const app = buildApp(); listening = new Promise(r => app.listen(8080, r)); } await listening; return inner.fetch(req, env, ctx); }`). Create the mysql connection inside the route handler and pass `disableEval: true` for `mysql2`.
docsImpact: On the Cloudflare guide's Vite Plugin page, state that database spans on Workers only exist when the Worker is built with `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` — a Worker deployed with plain `wrangler dev`/`wrangler deploy` emits no db spans and logs no warning — and correct the page to the shipped option shape (top-level `buildTimeInstrumentation` and `autoInstrumentation`, both default `true`, not `_experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection`/`_experimental.autoInstrumentation` defaulting to `false`); add that with build-time instrumentation on, an Express app must register its routes inside the request handler rather than at module scope, or the Worker fails to start with "Disallowed operation called within global scope".

When running Express behind `httpServerHandler` from `cloudflare:node`, add `setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` after your routes and before `app.listen()` to have route errors reported as unhandled; import it from `@sentry/server-utils` (add it as a dependency) because `@sentry/cloudflare` does not re-export it, so the `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` form shown on the Express guide is `undefined` in a Worker.

The Cloudflare guide has no page on running a Node HTTP framework behind `httpServerHandler` from `cloudflare:node` - `httpServerHandler` appears nowhere under ~/dev/sentry-docs, and `patchExpressModule` appears nowhere either. Add to docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/nodejs-compat.mdx: "Express, Koa and other Node HTTP frameworks running behind `httpServerHandler` are only instrumented when the code transform is active. With the Vite plugin (`sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()`, `buildTimeInstrumentation` on by default) you get framework spans and parameterized transaction names (`GET /users/:id`, `source: route`) automatically. Building with plain `wrangler dev`/esbuild instead gives no transform: the server span is then named after the raw URL under `traceLifecycle: 'static'` or after the method alone under `'stream'`. In that setup call `patchExpressModule(express, () => ({}))` from `@sentry/core/server` before creating the app - note it only renames the server span when span streaming is enabled."

The Deno guide must state that `@sentry/deno` does not instrument outgoing `fetch` out of the box: only `node:http`/`node:https` client calls get `http.client` spans and `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, so a handler that calls `fetch()` starts a new trace downstream unless you register a fetch integration yourself (`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/` currently has only `index.mdx` plus `configuration/integrations/{breadcrumbs,contextlines}.mdx`, and the breadcrumbs page's `fetch` option is the single mention of fetch anywhere in the guide, which reads as if fetch were instrumented).

REFUTED. The Bun plugin build is NOT required for db spans on Fastify + Bun. The reported "partial" is driver-specific, not a Bun/Fastify limitation: `mysql@2` needs the bundle, `mysql2 >= 3.20.0` does not.

EXACT CHANGE: use `mysql2` (tested 3.24.3) instead of `mysql@2.18.1`. Nothing else changes — same `instrument.mjs`, same `import "./instrument.mjs"` first line, plain `bun app.mjs`, no `Bun.build`, no `sentryBunPlugin()`.

Why: `mysql2 >= 3.20.0` publishes native `node:diagnostics_channel` channels (`mysql2:query`, `:execute`, `:connect`, `:pool:connect`). `mysql2Integration` in `@sentry/server-utils` subscribes to them EAGERLY in `setupOnce()` (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql2/index.ts:149-166), so no require-hook and no build-time channel injection is involved. `mysql@2` has no native channels, so it only works through the orchestrion transform that `@sentry/bun/plugin` applies at bundle time — which is exactly what the repo's own e2e app does (dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/bun-mysql/{build.ts,src/app.ts}, `mysql: 2.18.1`, `bun run dist/app.js`).

  GET /db-mysql2-query  | ["handler GET /db-mysql2-query","handler fastify - route-handler","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]
  GET /db-mysql2-execute| ["handler GET /db-mysql2-execute","handler fastify - route-handler","db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ?"]

workaround: Use `mysql2` (>= 3.20.0) rather than `mysql@2`. Create the connection or pool at module scope (or lazily — either works), keep `import "./instrument.mjs"` as the first line of the entry, and run `bun app.mjs` with no build step; db spans appear under the Fastify handler spans in both `stream` and `static` trace lifecycles. If you are stuck on `mysql@2`, the bundle really is required: `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ["./app.mjs"], outdir: "./dist", target: "bun", external: ["@sentry/bun", "mysql"], plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` then `bun dist/app.js` — the plugin strips instrumented packages back out of `external` so `mysql` gets bundled and transformed. Registering `sentryBunPlugin()` as a runtime `Bun.plugin` via `--preload` is not an alternative; it breaks `mysql`'s CJS default export.
docsImpact: The Bun guide needs a "Database instrumentation" section stating: libraries that publish native `diagnostics_channel` events — `mysql2` 3.20.0 and newer — are instrumented by a plain `bun app.js` run with no build step, while libraries without native channels — `mysql` v2 among them — are only instrumented when the app is bundled with `Bun.build` and `sentryBunPlugin()` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` (listing the package in `external` is fine, the plugin removes instrumented packages from that list so they are still transformed); registering that plugin at runtime through `Bun.plugin()` in a `--preload` file does not work and breaks CommonJS default exports. This also contradicts the current text at ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx:98 ("Sentry's auto-instrumentation does not work with bundled code... you'll need to manually instrument your code"), which is now backwards for library spans: on this SDK line bundling with the Sentry plugin is what turns library auto-instrumentation on, and that line must be rewritten rather than left alongside the new section.

The Deno SDK does not instrument outgoing `fetch()` calls: no `http.client` span is created and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers are attached, so distributed tracing stops at the Deno service — until this is fixed, either send outgoing requests through `node:http` (which is instrumented), or enable fetch tracing yourself by passing a fetch integration to `Sentry.init({ integrations: [...] })`.

Fresh (2.x) catches every error thrown in a route handler or middleware inside its own `App.handler()` and renders its 500 page, so the error never reaches `Bun.serve` and Sentry cannot capture it automatically: add `Sentry.captureException(ctx.error, { mechanism: { type: "fresh._error", handled: false } })` to `routes/_error.tsx` (or to `app.onError("*", ...)`) to report unhandled route errors, and note that the request span is still reported with status `internal_error` either way. There is no Fresh guide under docs/platforms/javascript/guides/ today and neither the Bun nor the Deno guide mentions Fresh, so this needs a new Fresh section rather than an edit.

details:
REFUTED. The "source is stuck on 'custom' in traceLifecycle 'static'" half of the partial verdict is an artifact of the original probe using the v10 attribute key. On develop (v11) the transaction source is read from `sentry.segment.name.source` (exported as `Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE` from `@sentry/bun`), not from `sentry.source`. `packages/core/src/tracing/sentrySpan.ts:451` does `const source = this._attributes[SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE]` and `packages/core/src/utils/spanUtils.ts:492-498` shows `updateSpanName()` deliberately stamps that attribute with 'custom'. Setting the correct key AFTER (or instead of) `updateSpanName` wins in both lifecycles.

The prior probe's middleware (variant A) set `rootSpan.setAttribute("sentry.source", "route")`, which on v11 is an unread attribute, so 'custom' stayed.

I re-ran the prior agent's own Fresh-on-bun app with four middleware variants x both lifecycles, plus a Bun.serve `routes` variant, against a local sink.

--- baseline, middleware present but no naming (VARIANT=NONE) ---
static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/42","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","trace_attrs":{"source_attr":"url"}}
stream: {"type":"span","raw":[{"name":"GET","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.bun.serve","source":"url"}]}
(confirms the out-of-the-box half of the claim; in stream the name is the bare method, not the URL)

--- A: Sentry.updateSpanName(root, name) + setAttribute("sentry.source","route")  [the prior probe] ---
static: {"name":"GET /users/:id","source":"custom","trace_attrs":{"source_attr":"custom","legacy_source_attr":"route"}}
stream: {"name":"GET /users/:id","is_segment":true,"source":"custom","custom_span_name":"GET /users/:id"}
Note: the prior report said stream reports source 'route' for this variant. It does not, it reports 'custom' there too. So variant A is worse than reported, and the working fix is the same in both lifecycles.

--- B: root.updateName(name) + setAttribute("http.route", route) + setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, "route")  [the fix, mirrors the SDK's own express patch-layer.ts:344-346] ---
static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_attrs":{"source_attr":"route","http_route":"/users/:id"}}
stream: {"type":"span","raw":[{"name":"GET /users/:id","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.bun.serve","source":"route","http_route":"/users/:id"}]}
error route, static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /boom","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"internal_error","trace_attrs":{"source_attr":"route","http_route":"/boom"}} followed by {"type":"event","exception":"Error: fresh-bun-route-boom","mechanism":"fresh.middleware","handled":false,"trace_id":"50561738703e4162a8f20be818c05e26"} on the same trace.

--- C: same as B plus "url.template" ---  identical to B (source 'route').
--- D: Sentry.updateSpanName(root, name) THEN setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, "route") ---
static: {"name":"GET /users/:id","source":"route","trace_attrs":{"source_attr":"route"}}
stream: {"name":"GET /users/:id","is_segment":true,"source":"route","custom_span_name":"GET /users/:id"}
So the order does not matter, only the key does. D additionally keeps `sentry.custom_span_name` so nothing downstream can rename it; B is the closer match to what the SDK's own framework integrations write.

--- E: no Sentry code in the app at all, Fresh route patterns registered on Bun.serve instead ---
Bun.serve({ port, routes: { "/users/:id": (req) => server.fetch(req) }, fetch: (req) => server.fetch(req) })
static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","trace_attrs":{"source_attr":"route"}}
This is fully automatic (bunserver.ts:206-218 parameterizes only when `request.params` is non-empty), but you must hand-enumerate every parameterized Fresh route, and a param-less route registered there still reports 'url'. Variant B is the practical answer.

- `wrangler.jsonc`: `"main": "dist3/worker.mjs"`, compat date 2026-05-01, `nodejs_compat`.

THE ONE NON-OBVIOUS BIT. A plain esbuild pre-bundle fails twice before it works, and both failures look like SDK bugs but are esbuild ESM-output artifacts:
1. `Error: Dynamic require of "diagnostics_channel" is not supported` on the first query — esbuild rewrites every `require()` of an external module in ESM output to its `__require` stub, and the orchestrion-injected snippet inside `node_modules/mysql/lib/Connection.js` requires `diagnostics_channel`.
2. Routing bare builtins through generated ESM shim modules instead (dist2) fixes that but then dies with `TypeError: The "superCtor.prototype" property must be of type object. Received undefined at Object.inherits (node:util:119:15) at node_modules/readable-stream/lib/_stream_readable.js` — `require('stream')` returned a namespace object, not the module.
The fix that works is a banner: statically `import * as __nbN from "node:<builtin>"` for every builtin the bundle asks for, then `globalThis.require = id => { const m = map[id.replace(/^node:/,"")]; return m.default !== undefined ? m.default : m; }`. esbuild's `__require` stub defers to a global `require` when one exists, so this restores correct CJS semantics. Builtins collected in this app: async_hooks, buffer, crypto, diagnostics_channel, events, fs, net, process, stream, string_decoder, timers, tls, url, util, zlib.

workaround: Two that work, both verified on Fresh 2.3.3 / wrangler 4.129.0 / @sentry/cloudflare 10.67.0. (a) Init-only, no framework file: add `integrations: [Sentry.captureConsoleIntegration({ levels: ["error"] })]` to the options `withSentry` returns; Fresh's DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER `console.error(error)`s the real Error, so the event carries the correct type, message and stack and shares the request's trace - the cost is that every other `console.error` in the app also becomes an issue, and the mechanism reads `auto.core.capture_console` / `handled: true`. (b) Explicit capture, better mechanism: either `routes/_error.tsx` with `Sentry.captureException(ctx.error, { mechanism: { type: "fresh", handled: false } })`, or a root middleware in main.ts before `app.fsRoutes()`: `app.use(async ctx => { try { return await ctx.next(); } catch (e) { Sentry.captureException(e, { mechanism: { type: "fresh", handled: false } }); throw e; } })` - the middleware form is preferable because it does not also have to render the 500 page and it still lets `routes/_error.tsx` produce the response. Both (a) and (b) also cover errors thrown while rendering a page component.
docsImpact: On Fresh 2 nothing that a route handler, middleware or page component throws ever reaches Sentry on its own: Fresh's default error handler catches it, `console.error`s it and returns a 500, so `withSentry` only marks the request span `internal_error` - either add `Sentry.captureConsoleIntegration({ levels: ["error"] })` to your `Sentry.init` options, which turns Fresh's own `console.error(error)` into a Sentry issue without touching any framework file (at the price of reporting every other `console.error` too), or capture explicitly in a root middleware (`app.use(async ctx => { try { return await ctx.next(); } catch (e) { Sentry.captureException(e); throw e; } })`) or in `routes/_error.tsx` via `Sentry.captureException(ctx.error)`.

On Cloudflare Workers the Sentry request span is named by HTTP method only (source "url"), so a Fresh guide must show a `main.ts` middleware that, in a `finally` around `ctx.next()`, calls `rootSpan.updateName(`${ctx.req.method} ${ctx.route}`)`, then `rootSpan.setAttribute("http.route", ctx.route)` and `rootSpan.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, "route")` — the source must be set after the rename because both `span.updateName()` and `Sentry.updateSpanName()` mark the name as "custom", and the `finally` is required because Fresh's error boundary sits outside user middleware, so a throwing route would otherwise keep the unparameterized name.

REFUTED. `mysql@2` db spans work on Fresh 2 / Deno 2.9.0 with @sentry/deno 10.67.0 (develop) in BOTH `vite dev` AND the production `deno task build` + `deno serve` shape, in both trace lifecycles. The report's "production build has no db span and the route 500s" is a vite-config problem, not an SDK or Fresh limitation.

THE EXACT CHANGE (vite.config.ts). The report used only `ssr: { external: ["mysql"] }`, which vite's build ignores because @fresh/plugin-vite sets `resolve.noExternal: true`. Adding a rollup external for the ssr *environment* does override it:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [fresh(), tailwindcss()],
  ssr: { external: ["mysql"] },                      // needed for vite dev
  environments: {                                     // needed for the build
    ssr: { build: { rollupOptions: { external: ["mysql"] } } },
  },
});
```

I isolated both knobs:
- `ssr.external` only -> build bundles the driver: `_fresh-route___api_db-aH-ILX-r.mjs 518.83 kB` plus rollup warnings `"default" is not exported by "node_modules/mysql/lib/protocol/Auth.js"` (this is the shape that 500s at runtime). ($D/buildB2.log)
- `environments.ssr.build.rollupOptions.external` only -> build externalizes: `_fresh-route___api_db-CSs3YcfK.mjs 0.85 kB`, and the chunk's first line is literally `import mysql from "mysql";`. ($D/buildB3.log)
- `environments...` only, no `ssr.external` -> vite DEV breaks: `ReferenceError: exports is not defined` on /api/db. So both lines are load-bearing, one per shape.

Setup reused (and extended) the earlier probe app at $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-fresh-deno-errors/app (Fresh 2.3.3 + @fresh/plugin-vite 1.1.2, deno 2.9.0, @sentry/deno 10.67.0 from develop in app/node_modules, traceLifecycle static, tunnel to my sink on 52117). CONFIRMED, no automatic capture. Baseline (no wiring), dev and prod, all three throw shapes:
  /api/boom -> 500 ; /api/boom2 -> 500 ; /throwpage -> 500
  tx | GET /api/boom | src= url | status= internal_error | trace= 809d5817
  tx | GET /api/boom2 | src= url | status= internal_error | trace= 96164bfa
  tx | GET /throwpage | src= url | status= internal_error | trace= 5bf72d3f
  event | sentinel | mech= generic handled= True
This is structural: jsr @fresh/core 2.3.3 src/app.ts App.handler() ends in `catch (err) { ctx.error = err; return await DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER(ctx); }`, so nothing escapes to Deno.serve/node:http. (Note the transaction status IS internal_error, so 500s are at least visible as failed transactions.)

REFUTED: the middleware is NOT the only mechanism. Four wirings all deliver the exception with the request's trace id, request data, and (in the built app) context lines, in BOTH `vite dev` and `deno serve _fresh/server.js`:

1) captureConsoleIntegration - init only, zero framework code, zero middleware. `integrations: [Sentry.captureConsoleIntegration({ levels: ['error'], handled: false })]`. It works because DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER does `console.error(error)` and core's console handler does `args.find(arg => arg instanceof Error)` -> captureException with the real stack.
  PROD: event | Error: fresh-deno-boom   | mech= auto.core.capture_console handled= False | ctxline= True | trace= 91440922
        event | Error: fresh-fsroute-boom | mech= auto.core.capture_console handled= False | ctxline= True | trace= f6f27fbc
        event | Error: fresh-render-boom  | mech= auto.core.capture_console handled= False | ctxline= True | trace= 11c92867
  DEV: same three, each on its transaction's trace (mech= auto.core.capture_console, tx= GET /api/boom etc.).
2) setErrorInterceptor from `jsr:@fresh/core@^2.3.3/internal` (public JSR export, `setErrorInterceptor(app, err => Sentry.captureException(err, ...))`, no ctx.next wrapping). Works in dev too even though @fresh/plugin-vite calls it per request - the compiled chain closes over the interceptor set at handler() time.
  PROD: event | Error: fresh-deno-boom | mech= fresh.errorInterceptor handled= False | ctxline= True | trace= 8800dad3 (+ the other two)
3) The reported try/catch middleware - reconfirmed, and it also covers fs routes and page renders, not just app.get routes (mech= fresh.middleware, all three, dev and prod).
4) routes/_error.tsx capturing `props.error` - works, but only for fs routes: /api/boom2 and /throwpage produced `mech= fresh._error`, /api/boom (registered via app.get, outside the fsRoutes segment) produced nothing.

NEW LIMITATION the report missed: any programmatic Fresh error handler silently kills mechanisms 1-3, including the reported middleware. With `app.onError("*", () => new Response("custom error page", { status: 500 }))` registered, prod runs produced ZERO events in every wiring:
  PROD captureConsole + error page  -> only tx rows + sentinel, no event (console.error is never reached)
  PROD setErrorInterceptor + error page -> only tx rows + sentinel, no event
  PROD middleware + error page      -> only tx rows + sentinel, no event (the error never reaches the outer catch)
Capturing inside the error handler itself is then the only option and does work: `app.onError("*", ctx => { Sentry.captureException(ctx.error, ...); return ... })` gave mech= fresh.onError for all three shapes in dev and prod. A file-based routes/_error.tsx behaves differently from app.onError: it renders the custom page AND the error still reaches an outer middleware, so combining the two double-captures (one of the two events is then dropped by the default dedupe integration - which one wins is not predictable).

ROOT CAUSE of "nothing about the framework is instrumented" (bonus, bears on the routenames/spans cells): Fresh 2 ships its own OTel instrumentation - src/otel.ts does `trace.getTracer("fresh", VERSION)` at module scope, compileMiddlewares wraps every chain in `tracer.startActiveSpan("middlewares", ...)`, `recordSpanError` calls `span.recordException(err)`, and App.handler does `span.updateName(`${method} ${pattern}`)` + `span.setAttribute("http.route", pattern)` on the active OTel span. @sentry/deno DOES register a global OTel provider (build/esm/opentelemetry/tracer.js: `setupOpenTelemetryTracer(){ trace.disable(); trace.setGlobalTracerProvider(new SentryDenoTraceProvider()); }`) and there is exactly ONE @opentelemetry/api copy (1.9.1) in the built bundle - yet no Fresh span ever arrives (`tx | GET /api/users/42 | spans= []`). My /api/otel probe pins the reason: a tracer obtained AFTER init works, one obtained BEFORE init is dead forever, because `trace.disable()` replaces the ProxyTracerProvider singleton and orphans every ProxyTracer handed out earlier:
  {"tracer":"SentryDenoTracer","earlyTracer":"ProxyTracer","earlySpan":"NonRecordingSpan","span":"SentrySpan","globalVersion":"1.9.1"}
(`span` = probe span started at request time -> real SentrySpan and it does show up: `tx | GET /api/otel | spans= ['probe-span']`; `earlySpan` = tracer captured in early.ts imported one line before instrument.ts -> NonRecordingSpan.) Fresh's module-level tracer is exactly this case, so all of Fresh's native spans and its http.route naming are silently discarded. Fixing Sentry.init to not orphan pre-existing tracers (or to set the delegate on the existing proxy provider) would light up Fresh middleware/render spans and route names for free. I could not find a user-side ordering fix: preloading with `deno serve -A --import=./instrument.ts _fresh/server.js` still left the pre-init tracer a NonRecordingSpan.

Not applicable/not tried: no Fresh e2e app exists in the repo (dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications has deno, deno-mysql, deno-pg, deno-redis, deno-streamed only, all raw Deno.serve), and ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/ has no Fresh page at all. All processes I started were killed; ports 52117-52119 are free.
workaround: Two-part wiring, both verified in `vite dev` and in the `deno serve _fresh/server.js` build. (a) If the app has no custom error handler, the cheapest capture is init-only, no framework code: `Sentry.init({ ..., integrations: [Sentry.captureConsoleIntegration({ levels: ['error'], handled: false })] })` in instrument.ts, imported as the first line of main.ts - Fresh's DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER console.errors every swallowed route, fs-route and render error and the integration turns it into a real exception event on the request's trace. (b) The moment the app registers an error handler (`app.onError("*", ...)`), that integration - and a try/catch middleware, and setErrorInterceptor - all go silent, so capture inside the handler instead: `app.onError("*", (ctx) => { Sentry.captureException(ctx.error, { mechanism: { type: 'fresh.onError', handled: false } }); return new Response("Internal server error", { status: 500 }); })`. A file-based routes/_error.tsx capturing props.error works too but covers only fs routes, not routes registered with app.get/post/etc. `setErrorInterceptor(app, err => Sentry.captureException(err, ...))` from `jsr:@fresh/core@^2.3.3/internal` is the least intrusive alternative to the try/catch middleware when there is no error handler.
docsImpact: A Deno/Fresh guide must say: Fresh catches every route, fs-route and render error inside `App.handler()` and answers with its own 500, so `Sentry.init()` alone reports nothing - add `captureConsoleIntegration({ levels: ['error'], handled: false })` for apps that use Fresh's default error page, and, if you register your own error handler (`app.onError` or `routes/_error.tsx`), call `Sentry.captureException(ctx.error, { mechanism: { type: 'fresh.onError', handled: false } })` inside that handler, because a custom error handler stops the console integration, a `ctx.next()` try/catch middleware and `setErrorInterceptor` from ever seeing the error; note also that Fresh's own OpenTelemetry spans and its `http.route` naming do not reach Sentry today, so transactions stay URL-named.

On Deno, request isolation is not guaranteed: Deno's `AsyncLocalStorage` restores the request's context into the root context when the handler awaits a dynamic `import()` (confirmed on Deno 2.9.0, for both `Deno.serve` and `node:http`, and not reproducible on Node), so data set with `Sentry.setTag`/`setUser`/`setContext`/`addBreadcrumb` during such a request is inherited by every later request; this hits any code-split server (Fresh 2's production build lazily imports each route chunk on its first request, so the first hit to each route leaks) and, until the runtime is fixed, the only reliable mitigation is a first middleware that strips tags, contexts, extra, user, breadcrumbs and attachments off `Sentry.getIsolationScope()` at the start of every request.

capability: outgoing fetch (http.client span + sentry-trace/baggage propagation) from a Fresh 2 route handler on Deno with @sentry/deno 10.67.0 (develop)
details:
Reproduced exactly, and it is a @sentry/deno gap (K2), not a Fresh gap. Probe dir: $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-fresh-deno-outgoingfetch (Fresh 2.3.3 + @fresh/plugin-vite 1.1.2, deno 2.9.0, SDK from $S/pack tarballs copied into app/node_modules). Two routes call out to a node:http recorder in the same request: /api/out uses global `fetch()`, /api/outnode uses `node:http.request()`. Driver: /run-b/drive.sh (sink 58101, recorder 58103, app 58105).

A) vite dev, traceLifecycle static, stock SDK (no extra integration):
  transaction | GET /api/out | op=http.server | src=route | spans=[]
  transaction | GET /api/outnode | op=http.server | src=route | spans=["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:58103/__rec"]
  REC: [{"url":"/__rec?via=fetch","sentry-trace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null},
        {"url":"/__rec?via=nodehttp","sentry-trace":"99f997b2...-a15eefd75fd6ddc5-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,...,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Foutnode,sentry-sampled=true,..."}]

D) production build (`deno task build` then `deno serve -A --port 58105 _fresh/server.js`), static, stock SDK, same result:
  transaction | GET /api/out | op=http.server | src=route | spans=[]
  transaction | GET /api/outnode | op=http.server | src=route | spans=["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:58103/__rec"]
  REC: [{"url":"/__rec?via=fetch","sentry-trace":null,"baggage":null,...}, {"url":"/__rec?via=nodehttp","sentry-trace":"b6219c48...-a725b91224d50651-1",...}]

So the only thing that fails is the global `fetch()`; `node:http` clients in the very same handler get an http.client span and both headers. Neither init placement, entry shape, nor lifecycle changes this: I tested vite dev and the bundled `_fresh/server.js`, and traceLifecycle static and stream. No variant of the framework wiring can fix it, because nothing in the request path is involved.

Root cause, verified in the source rather than guessed: `@sentry/deno` has no fetch tracing integration at all. Its default integration list (packages/deno/src/sdk.ts getDefaultIntegrations) contains denoServeIntegration + denoHttpIntegration, and denoHttpIntegration (packages/deno/src/integrations/http.ts) subscribes only to the `node:http` diagnostics channels (getHttpClientSubscriptions / HTTP_ON_CLIENT_REQUEST), which Deno's native `fetch` never goes through. Nothing named `fetchIntegration` is exported from packages/deno/src/index.ts. Notably the monkey-patch itself works fine on Deno: the default `breadcrumbsIntegration` (packages/deno/src/integrations/breadcrumbs.ts:47) already calls `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` for fetch breadcrumbs. What is missing is a handler that calls `instrumentFetchRequest`, i.e. exactly the file `@sentry/cloudflare` already ships at packages/cloudflare/src/integrations/fetch.ts.

I proved that by porting it into user land and re-running the same probe (app/fetch-tracing.ts, enabled by SENTRY_FETCH_TRACING=1):

B2) vite dev, static, with the integration:
  transaction | GET /api/out | op=http.server | src=route | spans=["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:58103/__rec"]
  REC: [{"url":"/__rec?via=fetch","sentry-trace":"c63d512111a8494fb8d0d3bf177b62d0-a23f474f5c9a1061-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=c63d512111a8494fb8d0d3bf177b62d0,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Fout,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rate=1",...}]

C) vite dev, traceLifecycle stream, with the integration:
  span | ["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","http.server GET /api/out"]

E) production build (`deno serve _fresh/server.js`), static, with the integration:
  transaction | GET /api/out | op=http.server | src=route | spans=["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:58103/__rec"]
  REC: [{"url":"/__rec?via=fetch","sentry-trace":"da5b6e985cf2498bb56030cb5e62c25d-9e6ddd7760f6588e-1","baggage":"...sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Fout,sentry-sampled=true,..."}]

Because a ~20-line user-land integration using only publicly exported `@sentry/core` APIs restores the span, the correct parent/child nesting and both headers in every shape, the gap is purely a missing default integration in `@sentry/deno`, not a Deno platform limitation. I did not exercise Deno's native `--unstable-otel` fetch instrumentation: it exports through Deno's own OTLP pipeline and shares no trace context with the Sentry SDK, so it cannot produce a child of the Sentry server span.

Repro: `cd app && SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:58101/ REC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:58103 SENTRY_LIFECYCLE=static SENTRY_FETCH_TRACING=0|1 deno task dev --port 58105`, then `curl /api/out /api/outnode /api/sentinel`. Logs in run-b/*.server.log; all servers I started are killed.
docsImpact: On the Deno platform page (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/), state plainly: "The Deno SDK does not create `http.client` spans for, or attach `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers to, requests made with the global `fetch()`; only `node:http`/`node:https` clients are instrumented, so a downstream service called with `fetch()` starts a new, disconnected trace." The same page's `breadcrumbs` integration doc (deno/configuration/integrations/breadcrumbs.mdx:23) already advertises fetch support for breadcrumbs, so the tracing exception has to be called out explicitly next to it, together with the user-land `instrumentFetchRequest` integration snippet as the interim workaround. Any Fresh/Deno framework guide should point at that Deno-level note rather than describing it as a framework limitation.

details:
Refutation attempt failed: no configuration of @sentry/deno 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) names a Fresh 2 route by itself. Both server shapes and both lifecycles still emit the raw URL, and app code is required in every case. I did find the exact root cause and a workaround that is smaller and better than the reported Fresh middleware.

Root cause (sharper than the original report). @sentry/deno DOES ship an OTel bridge: `init()` calls `setupOpenTelemetryTracer()` unless `enableOpenTelemetrySetup: false` (app/node_modules/@sentry/deno/build/esm/sdk.js:48-50 -> build/esm/opentelemetry/tracer.js). It calls `trace.disable()` and `trace.setGlobalTracerProvider(new SentryDenoTraceProvider())`, so `trace.getTracer(...).startSpan()/startActiveSpan()` DO produce real Sentry spans - I see Fresh's own `via-tracer`/`handler` spans arriving. What it does not install is an OTel ContextManager, so `context.active()` is still the NoopContextManager and `trace.getActiveSpan()` returns undefined. Fresh 2's router (jsr @fresh/core 2.3.3 src/app.ts:444-448: `const span = trace.getActiveSpan(); if (span && pattern) { span.updateName(`${method} ${pattern}`); span.setAttribute("http.route", pattern); }`) therefore no-ops. The SDK's own JSDoc for `enableOpenTelemetrySetup` admits the gap: "This does not handle custom context handling, it will always work off the current scope." The prior report's "@opentelemetry/api resolves to the NoopTracer" is half right: the tracer is Sentry's, the CONTEXT is noop.

Baseline (unchanged, my run) - vite dev, static:
  transaction | GET /api/users/42 | op=http.server | src=url | route=None | segsrc=url  spans= []
  transaction | GET /api/boom | op=http.server | src=url | route=None | segsrc=url  spans= []
Baseline - `deno serve _fresh/server.js` build, static: identical (`GET /api/users/42 | src=url | route=None`).

Working workaround, no Fresh middleware at all - register an OTel ContextManager in instrument.ts that resolves the SPAN key to the active Sentry root span (mode `ctxmgr-route`, app/instrument.ts). Fresh's built-in call then does all the naming:
  vite dev, static:  transaction | GET /api/users/:id | op=http.server | src=route | route=/api/users/:id | segsrc=route
  vite dev, stream:  span | http.server | GET /api/users/:id | src=route | route=/api/users/:id | seg=True
  deno serve build, stream: span | http.server | GET /api/users/:id | src=route | route=/api/users/:id | seg=True
  deno serve build, static: transaction | GET /api/users/:id | op=http.server | src=custom | route=/api/users/:id (mode `ctxmgr`, the plain variant)
The plain bridge (return the Sentry root span object as-is, mode `ctxmgr`) already gives `GET /api/users/:id` + `http.route` but leaves `src=custom`, because core's `updateName` marks the source custom. Wrapping the span so that `setAttribute("http.route", ...)` also sets `sentry.segment.name.source: "route"` upgrades it to `src=route`. Child spans (`custom work`, `via-tracer`) still nest correctly under the segment with the bridge installed.

Also re-checked and ruled out: `Deno.telemetry.contextManager` as the global context manager (mode `denootel`) - Deno's context never holds a Sentry span because the SDK called `trace.disable()`, so getActiveSpan stays undefined; there is no Fresh guide in ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/ (only `deno/index.mdx` + `deno/configuration`), and no Fresh e2e app in dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications (only deno, deno-mysql, deno-pg, deno-redis, deno-streamed), so there is no documented wiring to fall back on.

Files (all under $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-fresh-deno-routenames/): app/instrument.ts (modes baseline | ctxmgr | ctxmgr-active | ctxmgr-route | denootel | middleware), app/main.ts, app/routes/api/{boom,child,sentinel}.ts, app/routes/api/users/[id].ts, sink2.mjs, report.py, run2.sh, runprod2.sh, drive2.sh, and the captured results out-base-static.txt, out-ctx-static.txt, out-ctx-stream.txt, out-ctxroute-static.txt, out-ctxroute-stream.txt, out-prod-base-static.txt, out-prod-ctx-static.txt, out-prod-ctxroute-stream.txt.
Rerun: `PORT=51477 node sink2.mjs &` then `./run2.sh <mode> <static|stream> <label>` (vite dev, port 51478) or `cd app && deno task build` + `./runprod2.sh <mode> <lifecycle> <label>` (deno serve, port 51479); each writes out-<label>.txt.
docsImpact: The Deno SDK's OpenTelemetry compatibility layer (`enableOpenTelemetrySetup`, on by default) installs a tracer provider only, not a context manager: spans started through `tracer.startSpan()`/`startActiveSpan()` become Sentry spans, but `trace.getActiveSpan()` from `@opentelemetry/api` always returns `undefined`, so framework code that renames the active span - Fresh 2 does exactly this to apply `GET /api/users/:id` and `http.route` - silently has no effect and your transactions keep the raw URL as their name (`source: url`); until the SDK bridges the OTel context, name the segment yourself from the framework's matched pattern (`Sentry.updateSpanName(Sentry.getRootSpan(span), ...)` plus `http.route` and `sentry.segment.name.source: "route"`), either in a framework middleware or in a small `context.setGlobalContextManager` bridge in your instrumentation file.

details:
REFUTED: db spans on Hapi + Cloudflare Workers do NOT need the Cloudflare Vite plugin. The real requirement is build-time orchestrion instrumentation from ANY of the SDK's bundler plugins. `@sentry/server-utils` ships `./orchestrion/{vite,rollup,esbuild,webpack,webpack-loader,bun}`; `@sentry/cloudflare/vite` is just `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` (vite) + the auto-instrument plugin. Pre-bundling the Worker yourself with esbuild + `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild`, then pointing wrangler at that bundle, gives the same db spans with no vite and no @cloudflare/vite-plugin installed.

Exact change (probe at $S/deep/verify4-M-hapi-cf-dbspans/run-b/):
  build.mjs:
    import { sentryOrchestrionPlugin } from '@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild';
    esbuild.build({ entryPoints:['./src/index.mjs'], outfile:'./dist/worker.mjs', bundle:true,
      format:'esm', platform:'node', target:'es2022', external:['cloudflare:*'],
      banner:{ js: <require shim, see below> }, plugins:[forceEsmServerUtils, sentryOrchestrionPlugin()] })
  wrangler.jsonc: { "main": "dist/worker.mjs", "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01",
    "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat","enable_nodejs_http_server_modules"] }
  Run: node build.mjs && npx wrangler dev --port 43231 --inspector-port 0

WITH the esbuild orchestrion plugin (sink /__items, traceLifecycle 'static', mysql@2 module-scope pool, query inside the Hapi handler):
  {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db/{id}","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","spans":["router GET /db/{id}","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]}
  {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /ok","op":"http.server","source":"route","spans":["router GET /ok"]}
Control, IDENTICAL bundle minus the plugin (`node build.mjs --no-orchestrion`, dist-plain/worker.mjs):
  {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /db/7","src":"url","spans":[]}
  {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /sentinel","src":"url","spans":[]}
So the plugin, not the banner shim or the entry shape, is what produces the span. Route names (source=route, `router` span) also come with it, so the reported "needs the Vite plugin for Hapi route names" is refuted by the same run.

Two gotchas found:
1. esbuild require shim is mandatory. Without a banner, esbuild rewrites the CJS `require()` calls left in Hapi/mysql/the injected orchestrion snippet into `__require()`, and workerd dies at startup:
   "service core:user:verify4-hapi-esbuild-nobanner: Uncaught Error: Dynamic require of \"node:async_hooks\" is not supported / at worker.js:33:50 in __require2"
   Fix: `banner.js` that statically imports the node builtins workerd provides and sets `globalThis.require = id => map[id]`. (build-nobanner.mjs reproduces the crash.)
2. The injected snippet's `import '@sentry/server-utils'` resolves to the CJS build under esbuild; a tiny onResolve plugin forcing `node_modules/@sentry/server-utils/build/esm/index.js` avoids that. `@sentry/server-utils` does NOT list `@apm-js-collab/code-transformer-bundler-plugins` as a dependency, but it is vendored into the tarball (build/esm/vendored/...), so no extra install is needed.

Also REFUTED, secondary: "mysql2 cannot be used on workerd". mysql2@3.24.3 works and is instrumented once you pass mysql2's own `disableEval: true` pool option:
  GET /db2/{id}      -> {"rows":[{"id":1,"name":"ada"},{"id":2,"name":"linus"}]}
  {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /db2/{id}","src":"route","spans":["router GET /db2/{id}","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]}
Without `disableEval` the same pool returns {"error":"Code generation from strings disallowed for this context"} — a mysql2 configuration issue, not an SDK or workerd-vs-Sentry limitation. Note the span is still emitted for the eval pool because the failure happens after the query span opens.

Still true from the original report: `npx wrangler dev` on unbundled source (wrangler's internal esbuild) produces no db span, and there is no supported way to add a plugin to wrangler's own bundler — so "plain wrangler build" remains broken. The reference e2e app (~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/cloudflare-orchestrion-mysql) only covers the vite path.

Probe files (node_modules removed; reinstall with `npm install $S/pack/sentry-{cloudflare,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry}-10.67.0.tgz @hapi/hapi@21 mysql@2 mysql2@3 wrangler@4 esbuild@0.25`):
  $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-hapi-cf-dbspans/run-b/src/index.mjs
  .../run-b/build.mjs, build-nobanner.mjs, wrangler.jsonc, wrangler.plain.jsonc, wrangler.nobanner.jsonc
  .../run-b/dev-b.log (with plugin), dev-plain.log (control), dev-c.log (mysql2), dev-nobanner.log (__require crash)
One environment note: the shared directory carried a stale `.wrangler/deploy/config.json` from an earlier run that silently redirected `wrangler dev` to a different, vite-built worker; I overwrote it per run so each result is against the bundle named in its wrangler config.
workaround: Bundle the Worker yourself before wrangler sees it: `import { sentryOrchestrionPlugin } from '@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild'` in an esbuild build (format esm, platform node, external ['cloudflare:*'], plus a banner that maps `require` to statically imported node: builtins), set wrangler `main` to the emitted bundle, and run `wrangler dev`. For mysql2 on workerd, pass `disableEval: true` to createPool/createConnection.
docsImpact: Database spans on Cloudflare Workers require build-time instrumentation from a Sentry bundler plugin, not the Vite plugin specifically: use `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` with Vite, or `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/{esbuild,rollup,webpack}` if you pre-bundle your Worker yourself and point wrangler's `main` at the output; wrangler's own bundler takes no plugins, so building straight from source produces no db spans. When pre-bundling with esbuild, add a banner that backs `require` with statically imported `node:` builtins, otherwise workerd fails at startup with `Dynamic require of "node:async_hooks" is not supported`. `mysql2` works on Workers when you pass `disableEval: true` to the connection or pool.

details:
CONFIRMED as reported for every documented wiring, but the root cause is now pinned and it is NOT in Sentry: it is a workerd `node:http` server-shim bug, and neutralising it makes the SDK's own `hapiIntegration()` capture the throw correctly.

Probe dir: $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-hapi-cf-errors/ (src/index.mjs, wrangler.jsonc, vite.config.mjs, node-control.mjs, devA.log = plain wrangler/esbuild, devE.log = vite + sentryCloudflareVitePlugin, sink.mjs on port 52413). node_modules removed after the run.

WHAT I VARIED (all still broken out of the box): plain wrangler/esbuild build; vite + `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({autoInstrumentation:false})`; `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and `'stream'`; module-scope vs. deferred route registration; `hapiIntegration()` present and installed. Only the two app-side workarounds below produce an event.

ROOT CAUSE. Instrumenting `request.raw.res` on workerd (compat flags `nodejs_compat`, `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules`, compat date 2026-05-01, workerd 1.20260903.1) shows the response emits `close` BEFORE `finish` and before `res.end()` is ever called:
  MARK onPreResponse /error/7 isBoom=true writableEnded=false
  MARK res 'close' +2ms writableEnded=false writableFinished=false endCalled=false
  MARK res.end() called +3ms writableEnded(native)=false
  MARK res 'finish' +3ms writableEnded=true
  MARK response-event /error/7 writableEnded=true writableFinished=true finalStatus=499 isBoom=true hasClose=undefined
Plain Node control (node-control.mjs, same hapi 21, same routes) emits only `finish`-first and gets it right:
  internal:handler,error
  ERROR-CHANNEL:boom-7:tags=internal,error
  response-event writableEnded=true finalResponseStatus=500

hapi's transmit registers `res.on('close', internals.end(env,'close'))` (node_modules/@hapi/hapi/lib/transmit.js:259). Because `res.writableEnded` is still false when that premature `close` fires, `internals.end` takes the client-disconnect branch and does `request._setResponse(new Boom('Request close', {statusCode: disconnectStatusCode /*499*/}))` (transmit.js:287-305). `Request._finalize()` (lib/request.js:506-521) then only emits the `request`/`error` podium event when `this.response._close && this.response.statusCode === 500 && this.response._error` — but `this.response` is now a bare 499 Boom (`finalStatus=499 hasClose=undefined`), so the `error` channel never fires. That is why `hapiIntegration()`'s listener, and any hand-rolled `{name:'request',channels:['error']}` listener, never runs on Workers. The HTTP status the client sees is still 500 (headers were already written), so the breakage is invisible.

FIX THAT WORKS (one ext, no Sentry change), on the vite build with `hapiIntegration()`:
  server.ext('onRequest', (request, h) => {
    const res = request.raw.res;
    const on = res.on.bind(res);
    res.on = (event, listener) => (event === 'close' ? res : on(event, listener));  // drop workerd's premature 'close'
    return h.continue;
  });
Sink, same request driven with and without it:
  transaction | GET /error/{id} | trace= 7693a9e1b1544188a72be3db1775ab65        <- no fix: transaction only, no event
  event | Error: hapi-cf-route-boom-43 | mech= auto.function.hapi | tx= GET /error/{id} | trace= 50aae58175cd4f72bd4b6f0c609233b5
  transaction | GET /error/{id} | trace= 50aae58175cd4f72bd4b6f0c609233b5
Stable over 3 consecutive requests (3/3 captured), `/ok` and `/sentinel` unaffected (200, status=ok), and identical under `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` (`event Error: hapi-cf-route-boom-32 | mech= auto.function.hapi` with the fix, nothing without). `Object.defineProperty(res,'writableEnded',{get:()=>true})` works equally well and is the more direct statement of the workerd defect.

BUILD CAVEAT: `hapiIntegration()` only ever attaches its listener when the orchestrion channels are injected. devE.log (vite + plugin): "Integration installed: Hapi" and "MARK BOOT handlerState=true". devA.log (plain wrangler/esbuild): "Integration installed: Hapi" but "MARK BOOT handlerState=false" — so on a plain wrangler build the res-`close` fix alone is not enough; you need the Vite plugin as well, or the onPreResponse workaround.

The prior agent's `onPreResponse` + `Sentry.captureException` also works and needs no monkey-patching, but produces a strictly worse event: `event | Error: hapi-cf-route-boom-42 | mech= hapi.onPreResponse | tx= None` — no transaction name (the SDK's own handler sets it from `request.route`), and the mechanism is hand-written.

Not a Sentry bug, and no compat flag fixes it: the workerd binary only offers `enable/disable_nodejs_http_server_modules`, `enable/disable_nodejs_http_modules`, `nodejs_compat_v2` — none change the close/finish ordering. This should be filed against workerd's `node:http` `ServerResponse` (emit `finish` before `close`, and have `writableEnded` true when `close` fires). It also silently corrupts hapi generally on Workers: every request, success or failure, ends with `request.response` rewritten to a 499 disconnect Boom, so `server.events.on('response')`, `onPostResponse` and `request.info.responded` all see a bogus disconnect.
workaround: Two, both app-side. Preferred (keeps the SDK's own capture, correct transaction name and `auto.function.hapi` mechanism, requires the Vite plugin so the hapi channels are injected): drop workerd's premature `close` event before hapi's transmit can see it — `server.ext('onRequest', (request, h) => { const res = request.raw.res; const on = res.on.bind(res); res.on = (e, l) => (e === 'close' ? res : on(e, l)); return h.continue; })`. Equivalent: `Object.defineProperty(request.raw.res, 'writableEnded', { configurable: true, get: () => true })` in the same ext. Fallback that works on a plain wrangler/esbuild build with no Sentry bundler plugin: `server.ext('onPreResponse', (request, h) => { const r = request.response; if (r?.isBoom) Sentry.captureException(r, { mechanism: { type: 'hapi.onPreResponse', handled: false } }); return h.continue; })` — right trace and request data, but no transaction name on the event.
docsImpact: On Cloudflare Workers, hapi's `request`/`error` event never fires because workerd's `node:http` `ServerResponse` emits `close` before `finish` (with `writableEnded` still false), which hapi reads as a client disconnect and turns every response into a 499 — so `Sentry.hapiIntegration()` captures nothing; until workerd is fixed, add `server.ext('onRequest', (request, h) => { const res = request.raw.res; const on = res.on.bind(res); res.on = (e, l) => (e === 'close' ? res : on(e, l)); return h.continue; })` (with the Sentry Cloudflare Vite plugin enabled so the hapi instrumentation channels are injected), or capture manually from `server.ext('onPreResponse')` when `request.response.isBoom`.

details:
The reported claim is half right and half too narrow. Confirmed: with no build-time instrumentation the transaction is the raw path. Refuted: Vite is NOT required, and route names are reachable in a plain wrangler build with ~4 lines of user code.
