capability: outgoing fetch (http.client span + sentry-trace/baggage propagation) from a @hapi/hapi 21.4 handler on Deno 2.9.0 with @sentry/deno on develop (10.67.0)
docsImpact: On Deno, the Sentry SDK does not instrument the global `fetch`: calls made with `fetch()` produce no `http.client` span and carry no `sentry-trace` or `baggage` header, so the downstream service starts a new trace. Only `node:http`/`node:https` client requests are traced and propagated, so either route outgoing calls through `node:http` or register a fetch integration built on `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest` from `@sentry/core`. This is independent of the web framework (Hapi, Koa, Oak, Hono all behave the same) and of `traceLifecycle`.

workaround: Two, and they are independent. (A) For route names only, no hook and no JSON fix needed — keep the documented wiring (`import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno"; Sentry.init(...)`) and add to the hapi server: `server.ext('onPreHandler', (request, h) => { const a = Sentry.getActiveSpan(); if (a) { const root = Sentry.getRootSpan(a); root.updateName(`${request.method.toUpperCase()} ${request.route.path}`); root.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, 'route'); root.setAttribute('http.route', request.route.path); } return h.continue; });` — the SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE line must come after updateName, which otherwise leaves source `custom`. Gives `GET /users/{id}` source `route` in static and `http.server GET /users/{id}` in stream. (B) For full hapi instrumentation (router span, db spans, unhandled route errors) you still need `import "@sentry/deno/import"` plus a JSON load hook in the same entry: `import * as Module from 'node:module'; import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'; import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'; Module.registerHooks({ load(url, ctx, next) { return url.endsWith('.json') ? { format: 'json', source: readFileSync(fileURLToPath(url), 'utf8'), shortCircuit: true } : next(url, ctx); } });` — it can be imported before or after `@sentry/deno/import`, order does not matter, but it must come before the app.
docsImpact: The Deno guide should state that `@sentry/deno` alone names server transactions from the URL (`GET /users/42`, source `url`) and that parameterized hapi route names require either a `server.ext('onPreHandler')` that calls `getRootSpan(getActiveSpan()).updateName('<METHOD> ' + request.route.path)` followed by `setAttribute(SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, 'route')`, or the `import "@sentry/deno/import"` instrumentation hook, which on Deno 2.9 additionally requires a user-registered `Module.registerHooks({ load })` that returns `{ format: 'json' }` for `.json` URLs, because Deno (denoland/deno#36240) otherwise compiles `require('*.json')` as JavaScript and @hapi/validate fails to load at import time.

On the Hono (Deno tab) and Deno guides, under tracing/distributed tracing: "On Deno, outgoing requests made with the global `fetch()` are not instrumented: they produce no `http.client` span and receive no `sentry-trace` or `baggage` header, so the downstream service starts a new trace. Only `node:http` / `node:https` clients are traced automatically, via `denoHttpIntegration`. To trace a `fetch()` call, either use a `node:http` client instead, or wrap the call in `Sentry.startSpan({ name: '<method> <route>', op: 'http.client' }, ...)` and attach the headers yourself with `Sentry.getTraceData()` — a manual span on its own does not propagate the trace."

workaround: Build the Koa app and call `app.listen()` inside the `fetch` handler instead of at module scope, and keep `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` at its defaults. Concretely: hoist `const inner = httpServerHandler({ port: 8080 })` to module scope (that is safe), but put `new Koa()`, every `app.use(...)`, the router wiring and `app.listen(8080)` behind a memoized `ensureApp()` that the handler awaits before delegating to `inner.fetch`. With mysql2, also pass `disableEval: true` to `createConnection`.
docsImpact: On Cloudflare Workers, do not create the Koa app or call `app.use()` / `app.listen()` at module scope: with the Sentry Cloudflare Vite plugin's build-time instrumentation the instrumented `app.use()` starts a span at worker startup and workerd rejects it with "Disallowed operation called within global scope"; build the app and call `listen()` inside the `fetch` handler (memoized), then delegate to the `httpServerHandler` object, and database spans (mysql, mysql2) plus parameterized route names work on both `stream` and `static` trace lifecycles.

REFUTED. Koa errors ARE captured automatically on Cloudflare with the develop SDK — no `app.on('error')` needed. The reporter's setup was missing the one thing that turns Koa instrumentation on in a Worker: the `@sentry/cloudflare/vite` plugin's build-time instrumentation. A plain `wrangler dev` on a hand-written `src/index.js` (esbuild, no Vite) can never instrument Koa, because on Cloudflare the koa integration is not in the default set at all — `getBaseDefaultIntegrations()` in packages/cloudflare/src/baseSdk.ts only adds `...getRegisteredChannelIntegrations()`, i.e. whatever the Vite plugin registered on `globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__.integrations` at build time. `koaIntegration` is wired for that path (packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/config/channel-integration-definitions.ts:48 `{ exportName: 'koaIntegration', modules: ['koa'] }`, config in packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/config/koa.ts), and the integration auto-attaches the error listener on koa's `callback` channel (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/koa/koa-error-handler.ts, `attachKoaErrorHandler`) with `mechanism: { type: 'auto.middleware.koa', handled: false }`, captured inside the stashed request span.

WHAT I MEASURED

Baseline (their shape: plain wrangler dev, no Vite plugin, no `app.on('error')`) — reproduces their finding exactly. `/integrations` probe route:

GET /boom/7 -> 500, sink after sentinel:

  (no event, no router span — matches the report)

Fix (Vite build with a bare `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()`, Koa app constructed inside the first `fetch`, still NO `app.on('error')`), stream lifecycle:
  {"integrations":[...,"Console","Koa","SpanStreaming"],"orchestrionIntegrations":["koa"],"koaHandlerAttached":true,"errorListeners":2}
  {"type":"event","exception":"Error: koa-cf boom","mechanism":"auto.middleware.koa","handled":false,"sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","runtime":"cloudflare","hasContextLine":false,"transaction":"GET /boom/:id","trace_id":"affae71abd4644fbac876e5514b8dce3","user":{"ip_address":"127.0.0.1"},"request":{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:44741/boom/7","method":"GET",...}}
  {"type":"span","trace_id":"affae71abd4644fbac876e5514b8dce3","items":["router /boom/:id","http.server GET /boom/:id"],"raw":[{"name":"/boom/:id","status":"error","parent_span_id":"8d121e57b9269ec5","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.http.koa"},{"name":"GET /boom/:id","status":"error","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.cloudflare"}]}
Same worker with `traceLifecycle: 'static'`:
  {"type":"event","exception":"Error: koa-cf boom","mechanism":"auto.middleware.koa","handled":false,...,"transaction":"GET /boom/:id","trace_id":"8467ce5819094f3bb99ba8d504647c47",...}
  {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /boom/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"8467ce5819094f3bb99ba8d504647c47","spans":["router /boom/:id"]}

So three of the reporter's sub-claims fall at once: the error arrives with no user code; the mechanism is `auto.middleware.koa` (not "whatever the user writes"); and the server span/transaction is route-named (`GET /boom/:id`, `source: "route"`), not method-only. `hasContextLine: false` still holds (no `context_line` frames in either shape). Event and span share the trace id in both lifecycles.

WHY THEIR VITE ATTEMPT LOOKED LIKE "DOES NOT BOOT" — and the one real constraint

With the plugin on and the Koa app built at module scope (`const app = new Koa(); app.use(router.routes()); app.listen(8080)` at top level), workerd refuses to start:
  service core:user:koa-cf-c: Uncaught Error: Disallowed operation called within global scope. Asynchronous I/O (ex: fetch() or connect()), setting a timeout, and generating random values are not allowed within global scope.
      at index.js:54314:34 in use
      at index.js:57063:5
Line 54314 is inside the instrumented `Application.prototype.use`: `tr_ch_apm$use.start.runStores(__apm$ctx, ...)`. So it is the injected `diagnostics_channel` `runStores` call in `app.use()` — reached because `hasSubscribers` is truthy on workerd's shim — that performs the disallowed global-scope operation, not `app.listen()`. I bisected this:
  - Vite + `cloudflare()` only, module-scope app: boots, `GET /users/42 -> {"id":"42"}`.
  - Vite + `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ buildTimeInstrumentation: false })`, module-scope app: boots, `{"id":"42"}`.
  - Vite + bare `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()`, module-scope app: the error above.
  - Vite + bare `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()`, app built inside `fetch`: boots and gives everything quoted above.
That constraint is real and undocumented, but it is a boot-shape bug in the injected `use` wrapper, not the absence of an error-capture mechanism.

REFUTED. Koa 3.2.1 + @koa/router 15.7.0 on Cloudflare Workers DOES produce parameterized route names with @sentry/cloudflare 10.67.0 from develop, in both trace lifecycles. Two things are needed together, and the original probe had exactly one of them wrong.

(1) Build through Vite with `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` (defaults are fine: `autoInstrumentation: true`, `buildTimeInstrumentation: true`). Its orchestrion transform injects `orchestrion:koa:use` / `orchestrion:koa:callback` diagnostics channels into the bundled `koa/lib/application.js` and registers the Koa channel-subscriber factory on `globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__`, which `withSentry` picks up: `Sentry Logger [log]: Integration installed: Koa` (wrangler-e.log). Plain `wrangler dev` on the raw entry (esbuild, no plugin) does no injection, so there is nothing that can ever know the matched route - that is the reported baseline, which I reproduced exactly.

(2) Build the Koa app INSIDE the fetch handler, not at module scope. This is why the reporter concluded the plugin "no longer boots". The exact workerd error from my reproduction (wrangler-b.log, module-scope `buildApp().listen(8080)` + plugin):
  service core:user:koa-cf-b: Uncaught Error: Disallowed operation called within global scope. Asynchronous I/O (ex: fetch() or connect()), setting a timeout, and generating random values are not allowed within global scope.
    at index.js:54321:34 in use
    at index.js:57078:7 in buildApp
The frame at index.js:54321 is the injected `return tr_ch_apm$use.start.runStores(__apm$ctx, () => {...})` inside `Application.use` - i.e. the *instrumented* `app.use()` is the disallowed global-scope operation, not `app.listen()`. Un-instrumented `app.use()` at module scope boots fine (variant A). Moving app construction into the handler removes the failure completely. This mirrors the comment in the repo's own e2e app dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/cloudflare-orchestrion-mysql/src/index.ts ("The connection is created inside the handler: workerd forbids I/O in global scope"); there is no Koa+Cloudflare e2e app to copy from.

docsImpact: On Cloudflare Workers, `@koa/router` route names (`GET /users/:id`, `http.route`, source `route`) require building the Worker through Vite with `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()`, which injects the Koa diagnostics channels at build time; and because the instrumented `app.use()` performs a disallowed operation in Worker global scope, the Koa app must be created inside the fetch handler (lazily, guarded by a module-level promise) rather than at module scope, otherwise the Worker fails to start with "Disallowed operation called within global scope".

workaround:
main.ts (the whole fix, both parts):

  import './instrument.ts';                       // Sentry.init - still first
  import { makeApp } from './app.ts';             // Koa + @koa/router load here, BEFORE the hook

  await import('@sentry/deno/import');            // hook registered late, so it never sees Koa's require('*.json')
  const mysql = (await import('mysql')).default;  // driver imported AFTER the hook -> instrumented

  const connection = mysql.createConnection({ host, port, user, database });  // NOT createPool
  connection.connect(err => err && console.error(err));
  makeApp(connection).listen(port);

Do not use `mysql.createPool`: pooled queries emit a db span in a detached trace of their own instead of on the request transaction. Everything else the original probe reported still holds - @sentry/deno has no `setupKoaErrorHandler`, so keep the hand-written `app.on('error', err => Sentry.captureException(err, { mechanism: { type: 'manual.koa.onerror', handled: false } }))`, and the server span is still named from the URL (static) or method-only (stream) because there is no Koa router integration.
docsImpact: On Deno, a Koa app cannot put `import "@sentry/deno/import"` first (Deno fails on `require('*.json')` inside Koa's `statuses` dependency, denoland/deno#36240): import your Koa app module first, then register the hook with a top-level `await import("@sentry/deno/import")` and dynamically `await import()` your database driver after it - and create the driver client with `mysql.createConnection`, since queries made through `mysql.createPool` produce a db span in a separate trace instead of on the request transaction.

On Deno, Koa needs build-time instrumentation instead of the `import "@sentry/deno/import"` runtime hook (which crashes Koa at import on Deno 2.9): bundle your server with esbuild using `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` — with `format: 'esm'`, `external: ['@sentry/deno', '@sentry/server-utils']` and a `createRequire` banner — and run the bundle with `deno run`; that gives you automatic Koa error capture (`auto.middleware.koa`), router spans, and parameterized route names with no `app.on('error')` of your own, and note that `@sentry/deno` does not export `setupKoaErrorHandler`.

details:
Reproduced the reported behavior exactly, and then made it work with a user-land integration, so the finding is real but its "no configuration exists" framing is too strong.

Root cause (source, not Koa): `@sentry/deno` ships NO fetch tracing integration. `packages/deno/src/sdk.ts` default integrations are eventFilters, requestData, functionToString, linkedErrors, dedupe, breadcrumbs, denoContext, denoServe, denoHttp, contextLines, normalizePaths, globalHandlers + server-utils error/tracing integrations. The only `fetch` code in `packages/deno/src` outside the transport is `integrations/breadcrumbs.ts` (breadcrumbs only). The built entry exports no fetch integration at all (grep of `build/esm/index.d.ts` for `*Integration` returns denoHttp/denoServe/denoKoa/... and nothing fetch-related). `denoHttpIntegration` subscribes only to `http.client.request.created` / `http.server.request.start` on `node:diagnostics_channel`, which Deno's native `fetch` never emits. Node's equivalent (`packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/`) is undici-based and does not apply to Deno. The repo's own e2e app confirms this is the intended state: `dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/deno/tests/fetch.test.ts` asserts only a span the app itself created with `Sentry.startSpan({name:'test-outgoing-fetch'})` and `origin: 'manual'` -- there is no assertion of an `http.client` span from fetch. Koa is irrelevant to the failure.

docsImpact: On Deno the SDK does not create spans for outgoing `fetch()` calls and does not attach `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers to them (only breadcrumbs are recorded); requests made through `node:http`/`node:https` are traced and propagated normally, so either use a `node:http`-based client or register a fetch integration in your own code with `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` and `instrumentFetchRequest` from `@sentry/core`. docsImpact: On Deno, Koa instrumentation (and with it the `http.route` attribute and the parameterized `GET /users/:id` transaction name) needs the Sentry import hook to be loaded through `deno run --import=./preload.ts` rather than as the first `import` of the entry file, because Deno loads the entry's whole static module graph, Koa included, before the entry's first statement runs, and that preload must register a `node:module` `registerHooks` load hook returning `.json` files with `format: "json"` first, otherwise Koa's `statuses` dependency aborts the process with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` (denoland/deno#36240).

Root cause of the partial: on Bun the route name comes only from the express instrumentation's `http.route`, which is injected at bundle time by sentryBunPlugin; without a bundle nothing patches Nest's express router, and the SDK prints no warning at all unless `debug: true` (v1-unbundled-static.log contains zero Sentry output).
workaround: Unbundled Bun can be given real route names from user code with a global Nest interceptor (src/route-name2.interceptor.ts + src/main-rename2.ts): read `req.route.path`, then on the root span call `updateName(`${req.method} ${route}`)`, `setAttribute('http.route', route)` and — this is the load-bearing part on develop — `setAttribute('sentry.segment.name.source', 'route')`. Static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route"}; stream: {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET /users/:id"]}. Setting the old `sentry.source` attribute instead does NOT work: `updateName()` calls INTERNAL_setSegmentNameSourceIfSegment(span,'custom') (packages/core/src/tracing/sentrySpan.ts:232) and the earlier interceptor variant that set `sentry.source` produced {"name":"GET /users/:id","source":"custom"}. The interceptor only fixes the name/source; the express `middleware`/`handler` child spans stay absent. The supported fix remains bundling with sentryBunPlugin.
docsImpact: A Bun + NestJS docs page must say: on Bun, NestJS route names (and the express middleware/handler child spans) only exist when you bundle your app with `Bun.build({ target: 'bun', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` and run the bundle — with plain `bun src/main.ts` the server span is `GET /users/42` with source `url` under `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and just `http.server GET` (no path at all) under the default `'stream'` lifecycle, with no warning unless `debug: true`; the build additionally needs `external: ['@nestjs/microservices', '@nestjs/microservices/microservices-module', '@nestjs/websockets', '@nestjs/websockets/socket-module', '@nestjs/platform-express/multer', 'class-validator', 'class-transformer', 'cache-manager']` or it fails with `error: Could not resolve: "@nestjs/microservices/microservices-module"`, and `Sentry.init` must come from `@sentry/bun` (initializing from `@sentry/nestjs`/`@sentry/node` on Bun yields no server spans at all). Note that the current Bun guide states the opposite of the develop behavior — ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx:98: "Sentry's auto-instrumentation does not work with bundled code ... If you need to bundle your application, you'll need to manually instrument your code" — and that sentence has to be replaced, not amended.

The reported "partial" rested on one claim: "mysql2 cannot run on workerd at all (EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed), only mysql@2 works". That is refuted. mysql2 has a first-class config flag, `disableEval: true` (mysql2 3.24.3, `lib/connection_config.js:62`, honored in `lib/commands/query.js:225` and `lib/commands/execute.js:39`), which switches the row parsers off the `new Function` path. With it, mysql2 runs on workerd and produces fully attributed db spans, including prepared statements via `.execute()`.

Same app, same wiring as the original probe (NestJS 11 + platform-express, `httpServerHandler` bridge, lazy Nest boot, esbuild + `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild`, wrangler 4.129.0 dev, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, `nodejs_compat` + `enable_nodejs_http_modules` + `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules`), only the driver config changed.

  /db2fresh-eval   (mysql2 createConnection, no flag)           -> {"ok":false,"err":"EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context | at Function (<anonymous>) | at line.toFunction (.../worker.js:140167:25)"}
  /db2exec         (mysql2 .execute prepared, disableEval)      -> {"ok":true,"rows":[{"id":1,"name":"ada"},{"id":2,"name":"linus"}]}
  /db2pool         (mysql2 createPool, disableEval)             -> rows on a cold isolate, see pool caveat below
  /db               (mysql@2 module-scope pool, baseline)       -> rows

Bundler/hook variant re-confirmed, not refuted: the same source built with `plugins: [processPlugin]` only (build-noorch.mjs -> dist-noorch, wrangler-noorch.jsonc) yields no db spans, no express spans and an unrouted server span:
  span ["http.server GET"]   <- /dbfresh and /db2fresh, no-orchestrion build
So `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` (or the Vite plugin's buildTimeInstrumentation) is genuinely required; that part of the original report stands.

New caveat the original report gets backwards (affects the query, not the span): module-scope connection pools are the wrong shape on workerd. The module-scope mysql2 pool intermittently fails with "Error: Cannot perform I/O on behalf of a different request. I/O objects ... created in the context of one request handler cannot be..." on requests that reuse a socket opened by an earlier request (rounds 1 and 3 of 3 failed, round 2 passed), and the module-scope mysql@2 pool the original probe recommends silently costs 10 seconds on every request after the first (measured `[10.012133s]`, `[10.008806s]`, `[10.007499s]` vs `[0.005991s]` for a per-request connection). A connection created inside the handler is fast and correct for both drivers, and still gets spans, because instrumentation is injected at bundle time, not at first module load (the Bun K11 "module scope only" rule does not apply here). The repo's own e2e app agrees: dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/cloudflare-orchestrion-mysql/src/index.ts creates the connection inside `fetch` with the comment "workerd forbids I/O in global scope, and mysql opens its socket lazily on the first query", and its tests assert `sentry.origin: auto.db.mysql`, `db.system.name`, `db.query.text`, `server.address/port`.

workaround: Use mysql2 with `disableEval: true` in the connection/pool options (`mysql2.createConnection({ host, port, user, database, disableEval: true })`); without it workerd throws `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context` from mysql2's generated row parsers. Open the connection inside the request handler rather than at module scope: a module-scope pool either fails with "Cannot perform I/O on behalf of a different request" (mysql2) or adds a silent ~10s per request (mysql@2). Spans are unaffected by where the connection is created because the orchestrion esbuild/Vite plugin injects the diagnostics channel at build time.
docsImpact: On Cloudflare Workers, `db` spans require the build-time orchestrion transform (`sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild`, or `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()`'s `buildTimeInstrumentation` for Vite builds) and work with both `mysql@2` and `mysql2` — for `mysql2` you must pass `disableEval: true` in the connection options, since workerd forbids code generation from strings — and the connection must be created inside the request handler, not at module scope, because workerd forbids reusing a socket across requests.

workaround: None needed. Use the SDK's own filter instead of a hand-written one: install `@sentry/nestjs` alongside `@sentry/cloudflare` and add to the root module `imports: [SentryModule.forRoot()]` and `providers: [{ provide: APP_FILTER, useClass: SentryGlobalFilter }]`, both from `@sentry/nestjs/setup`. Nothing in `src/main.ts` changes. For error capture alone the `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` esbuild plugin can also be dropped; keep it only if you want express middleware/handler spans and `source: "route"` transaction names.
docsImpact: On Cloudflare Workers, NestJS error capture uses the same wiring as on Node: install `@sentry/nestjs` next to `@sentry/cloudflare` and register `SentryGlobalFilter` from `@sentry/nestjs/setup` as an `APP_FILTER` provider (with `SentryModule.forRoot()` in `imports`) in your root module - `@sentry/nestjs/setup` depends only on `@nestjs/*` and `@sentry/core`, so it reports through the Cloudflare client and yields events with mechanism `auto.http.nestjs.global_filter`, `handled: false`, correct trace linking and request context, while expected `HttpException`s are not reported. No hand-written `@Catch()` filter is required, and the `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` esbuild plugin is only needed for library spans, not for error capture.

capability: db spans (Next.js 15.5.4 app router, @sentry/nextjs 10.67.0 develop, bun 1.4.0 via `bun --bun next build/start`)
details:
REFUTED. db spans do arrive on Next.js + bun, for both mysql2 and ioredis, with the reporter's exact wiring plus one six-line addition to `sentry.server.config.ts`. No import hook, no `NODE_OPTIONS`, no `--preload`, no `serverExternalPackages` change and no bundling change is needed.

The reporter's diagnosis was wrong on the mechanism. mysql2 3.24.3 (and ioredis 5.11.1) publish their own `node:diagnostics_channel` events natively; the SDK subscribes to `mysql2:query`/`:execute`/`:connect`/`:pool:connect` in `redis/mysql2` `setupOnce`, and mysql2 staying a bare external `require("mysql2/promise")` is irrelevant — `registrationOnly({ name: 'mysql2', versionRange: '>=3.20.0' })` in `packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/config/mysql2.ts` means no code injection is wanted for that version. The real defect is that **bun garbage-collects the diagnostics_channel Channel objects that only Sentry's subscriber references**, so every channel-based subscription made by `Sentry.init()` is gone one tick later.

Proof, plain bun + `@sentry/node`, no Next.js (`app/t-probe4.mjs`):
```
sync subs= true
t50 subs= false
after import subs= false
after cmds subs= false
```
Holding a strong reference (`app/t-probe5.mjs`) fixes it:
```
sync subs= true
t50 subs= true
{"type":"transaction","name":"probe-keepref","op":"test",...,"spans":["db.query redis-get"]}
```
The identical script on node v26.5.0 already worked (`"spans":["db.query redis-set"]`, `"spans":["db.query redis-get"]`), so this is bun-specific.

A/B on one and the same Next.js production build (`bun --bun ./node_modules/.bin/next start -p 41778`), driven by curl:

CONTROL, `SENTRY_NO_PIN=1` (the pin dropped right after init) — reproduces the report exactly:
```
{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /app/api/db","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /app/api/db/route","start response"]}
{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /app/api/redis","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /app/api/redis/route","start response"]}
```
FIXED, same build, pin kept:
```
{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /app/api/db","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /app/api/db/route","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users","start response"]}
{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /app/api/redis","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /app/api/redis/route","db.query redis-set","db.query redis-get","start response"]}
```
`traceLifecycle: 'stream'` works too, with the correct origin:
```
{"type":"span","items":["resolve page components","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users"],"raw":[...,{"name":"SELECT users","origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel"}]}
{"type":"span","items":["resolve page components","db.query redis-set","db.query redis-get"],"raw":[...,{"name":"redis-set","origin":"auto.db.redis.diagnostic_channel"}]}
```

Two of the reporter's observations are real but harmless: `[Sentry] Runtime hook not registered` is correct and unavoidable (bun 1.4.0 has no `Module.registerHooks`, and `packages/server-runtime-injection/src/register.ts` deliberately excludes Bun from the `Module.register` path), and `injected libraries=[]` is correct because mysql2 needs no injection at that version. Both are red herrings for db spans on a modern driver. They do matter for drivers below the native-channel cutoff (mysql2 < 3.20.0, ioredis < 5.11.0, mysql, pg, mongodb, ...): those need injection, and on Next.js only `ioredis` is un-externalized for build-time injection (`BUNDLE_SAFE_INSTRUMENTED_PACKAGES = ['ioredis']` in `packages/nextjs/src/config/diagnosticsChannelInjection.ts`), so old-driver spans on Next.js + bun stay unreachable — that part of the report stands.

Underlying SDK bug worth filing: `subscribeRedisDiagnosticChannels` / the mysql2 equivalent discard the handle returned by `bindTracingChannelToSpan`, so nothing holds a strong reference to the channels. Node's GC happens not to collect them in practice; bun's does, within one tick. A module-scope array of the subscribed channels inside `@sentry/server-utils` would fix it for every bun user without any app change.

Not run: bun 1.3.14 (the CI pin) — `$S/bun1314` does not exist on this machine.

Files: $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-nextjs-bun-dbspans/ (REPRO.md, app/, server1.log, server6.log, server8-nopin.log, server9-stream.log). Ports 41777 sink, 41778 app, 41779 redis. Redis container `deep-verify4-nextjs-bun-redis` started from redis:7-alpine and stopped again; all processes killed.
docsImpact: On Bun, keep a strong reference to the diagnostics channels after `Sentry.init()` — e.g. `globalThis.__sentryKeptChannels = ['mysql2:query','mysql2:execute','mysql2:connect','mysql2:pool:connect','ioredis:command','ioredis:connect'].map(n => require('node:diagnostics_channel').tracingChannel(n))` — otherwise Bun garbage-collects the channels Sentry subscribed to and database spans stop being recorded, even though the driver is instrumented and the SDK reports no error; this applies to any Bun-hosted app including Next.js run with `bun --bun next start`, and needs drivers new enough to publish native channels (mysql2 >= 3.20.0, ioredis >= 5.11.0, node-redis >= 5.12.0), since older drivers additionally need the runtime module hook that Bun cannot register.

details:
REFUTED. The claim reproduces exactly with the reported wiring, but it is a missing-integration problem, not a platform limitation. Adding `fetchIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` to `Sentry.init` in `sentry.server.config.ts` restores both the `http.client` span and the propagation headers, under BOTH trace lifecycles.

Probe dir: $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-nextjs-bun-outgoingfetch/ (REPRO.md, sink.mjs, recorder.mjs, app/, server-baseline.log, server-fix.log, server-stream.log; app/node_modules removed after the run, REPRO.md has the reinstall line).

BASELINE (no fetchIntegration, traceLifecycle 'static') - reproduces the report:
  recorder /__hits: {"url":"/hit","sentry-trace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null}

  Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static', integrations: [fetchIntegration()] });

  The header's span id (9987b591f02565e2) and trace id match the emitted http.client span exactly, so the downstream service continues the same trace.

  recorder: "sentry-trace": "aa02efe64b2e4b9bb7a5c77e35a85235-95cf1f8492e6e32d-1", baggage present

Its sentry.server.config.ts imports `bunHttpServerIntegration` and `fetchIntegration` from `@sentry/bun` next to `Sentry.init` from `@sentry/nextjs`, its package.json lists `@sentry/bun` as a dependency, and tests/propagation.test.ts asserts the http.client span id equals the downstream `sentry-trace` span id. So the SDK ships and tests this combination; only the docs are silent.

Everything else the report says about the wiring held: `withSentryConfig` is only on `@sentry/nextjs/config` on develop, `bun --bun` is required, `contexts.runtime` is still {"name":"node","version":"v26.3.0"}-style (my sink showed runtime "node"). Rename it to anything else (`web`, `my-app`, the project name) and rebuild — route names come out as `GET /api/users/[id]` with `transaction_info.source: "route"`, and events and transactions carry the same name. Net: on Next.js/OpenNext/workerd you get db spans only for drivers that publish their own diagnostics channels (mysql2 does; `.open-next/server-functions/default/node_modules/mysql2/lib/tracing.js`). workaround: For mysql2 on Cloudflare Workers, pass mysql2's own `disableEval: true` in the connection/pool options (`mysql2.createPool({ host, port, user, database, disableEval: true })`). workerd forbids `new Function`, and mysql2 compiles its row parsers that way; `disableEval` switches it to the static parsers, after which the query returns rows (HTTP 200) and the `db mysql2.pool.connect` / `db mysql2.connect` / `db SELECT <table>` spans arrive unchanged. This is app-side driver config, no Sentry option involved. There is no workaround for mysql@2 (or any driver without built-in diagnostics channels): the runtime module hook cannot register on workerd, and pulling mysql into the webpack bundle via `serverExternalPackages` yields spans but breaks the driver with PROTOCOL_INCORRECT_PACKET_SEQUENCE even with Sentry's build-time instrumentation disabled.
docsImpact: On docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nextjs.mdx (which today ends at "you should start seeing error events, traces, and logs"), add: "Database spans on Workers only come from drivers that publish their own diagnostics channels, such as mysql2; drivers instrumented through Sentry's runtime module hook (for example mysql 2.x) produce no spans there, because the hook cannot register on workerd. With mysql2, also pass `disableEval: true` in your connection options — the Workers runtime forbids `new Function`, which mysql2 otherwise uses to build its row parsers."

RUN 1 - documented wiring (sentry.server.config.BASELINE-broken.ts, traceLifecycle 'static'). CONFIRMS THEIR CLAIM, build1.log / wrangler1.log:
  outfetch: {"ok":true,"where":"outfetch","rec":"recorded"}

No http.client span, no headers, for either fetch() or node:http. The newer compat date and global_fetch_strictly_public change nothing.

ROOT CAUSE (read in the SDK, not guessed): packages/nextjs/src/server/index.ts:138-183 - on OpenNext/Cloudflare the SDK only swaps contexts.runtime to 'cloudflare' and the sdk metadata to ['nextjs','cloudflare'], then still calls `nodeInit` from @sentry/node. Outgoing HTTP therefore depends on @sentry/node's undici/NodeFetch + node:http instrumentation, which patches an undici instance that workerd's global fetch is not. @sentry/cloudflare's runtime-agnostic `fetchIntegration` (packages/cloudflare/src/integrations/fetch.ts, a `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest` wrapper around globalThis.fetch) is never installed on this path, and @sentry/cloudflare is not even a dependency of @sentry/nextjs.

RUN 2 - REFUTATION, one added integration (sentry.server.config.FIXED.ts, traceLifecycle 'static'), build2.log / wrangler2.log:

  {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/outhttp","op":"http.server",...,"spans":[...,"http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:47312/__rec","start response"]}
  recorder: [{"url":"/__rec?from=outfetch","sentry-trace":"2e8013c474304c9a8b39a312e043d7bf-994b6fc4ac6ed8cd-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=2e8013c474304c9a8b39a312e043d7bf,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Foutfetch,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rand=0.487...,sentry-sample_rate=1"}, {"url":"/__rec?from=outhttp","sentry-trace":"d5cf36e31b094b009c23b139cca54e1c-8f16fc134f5cc807-1","baggage":"...sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Fouthttp..."}]
The trace_id in the header matches the transaction's trace_id, so the span is correctly parented. node:http is fixed too, because unenv routes node:http through global fetch.

RUN 3 - same fix with traceLifecycle 'stream' and NO tracePropagationTargets (build3.log / wrangler3.log), to show neither is load-bearing:
  {"type":"span","trace_id":"eb26125052c74a71a6fc4e88f42e0ab6","items":["resolve page components","http.client GET 127.0.0.1"],"raw":[...,{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"9914b3dac32a2e3f","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.http.fetch"}]}

WHAT I ALSO CHECKED (all negative as fixes on their own): the newer/stricter wrangler compat pair from the repo e2e app; traceLifecycle 'static' vs 'stream'; the docs page's own compatibility_date >= 2025-08-16 advice (that is about https.request for the transport, not about client spans).

REFERENCE APP: ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/nextjs-16-cf-workers uses exactly the documented wiring (instrumentation.ts -> sentry.server.config.ts, withSentryConfig from '@sentry/nextjs/config', defineCloudflareConfig()) and asserts nothing about server-side outgoing HTTP. Its only 'http.client' assertion (tests/prefetch-spans.test.ts:19) is a browser-side prefetch span. So this gap is uncovered by the repo's own e2e suite.

Verdict is `partial` and not `works-after-all` because the default and documented setup really does produce zero outgoing-HTTP telemetry, exactly as reported; it is `partial` and not `confirmed-broken` because a one-line, public-API change fully restores spans and header propagation for both fetch() and node:http, under both trace lifecycles.

DOCS PAGE: ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nextjs.mdx covers only nodejs_compat and compatibility_date, and closes with "You should start seeing error events, traces, and logs appear in Sentry." It never mentions that outgoing HTTP is uninstrumented there.
docsImpact: On docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nextjs.mdx, after the Wrangler section: "On Cloudflare Workers the Next.js SDK cannot instrument outgoing HTTP requests automatically, because the Workers runtime provides a native `fetch` rather than the Node.js `undici` implementation the SDK patches. Requests you make from Server Components, route handlers, or Server Actions will produce no `http.client` span and will not carry `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, so the trace stops at your Worker. To get them, install `@sentry/cloudflare` and add its `fetchIntegration()` to your `sentry.server.config.ts`: `import { fetchIntegration } from '@sentry/cloudflare'; Sentry.init({ /* ... */ integrations: [fetchIntegration()] });` This also covers `node:http` calls, which the Workers Node compatibility layer routes through `fetch`."

capability: db spans (Next.js 15.5.4 App Router route handlers on Deno 2.9.0, develop/10.67.0)
details:
Still partial, but the reported *reason* ("no instrumentation path is available" / "buildTimeInstrumentation ... does not transform externalized node_modules deps") is REFUTED. Build-time instrumentation works under Deno and produces real db spans for the driver Sentry un-externalizes for exactly that purpose.

Probe: $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-nextjs-deno-dbspans (see RERUN.txt for every command; node_modules removed after the run). Wiring identical to the reported one (next.config.mjs default-interop `@sentry/nextjs/config`, instrumentation.js, sentry.server.config.js with `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false`, tunnel to a local sink), plus `ioredis@5.4.1` (below 5.11, i.e. no native diagnostics_channel, injection-dependent), `mysql2@3.24.3`, `mysql@2.18.1`, all clients created at module scope in lib.js.

A. `deno run -A node_modules/next/dist/bin/next build` + `... next start -p 41338`, default externals, runtime hook OFF, traceLifecycle 'static'. Build succeeded on Deno; `.next/server/chunks/{330,394,829}.js` contain `orchestrion:ioredis` (the webpack orchestrion loader transformed the bundled ioredis at build time). Sink:
  transaction "GET /api/dbredis" spans: ["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /api/dbredis/route","db.query set probe:key [1 other arguments]","db.query get probe:key","start response"]
  transaction "GET /api/dbmysql2" spans: ["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /api/dbmysql2/route","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users","start response"]
  transaction "GET /api/dbmysql" spans: ["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /api/dbmysql/route","start response"]   <- mysql@2: no span (confirms that half)
All routes 200.

B. traceLifecycle 'stream', same build: span envelopes carry the same ioredis spans, so the lifecycle is not the variable.
  span ["resolve page components","db.query set probe:key [1 other arguments]","db.query get probe:key"]
  span ["resolve page components","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users"]
  span ["resolve page components"]   <- the mysql@2 request

C. Default docs wiring (RUNTIME_INJECTION=1, i.e. no `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false`) reproduced exactly as reported: server-hook.log:7 "Registered diagnostics-channel injection via Module.registerHooks()", then every route 500s with "⨯ SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'" (hello=500 dbredis=500 dbmysql2=500 dbmysql=500).
   New, sharper evidence that this is a plain Deno bug and not Sentry's transform: minhook/main.cjs registers a *pass-through* `Module.registerHooks({resolve: next-through, load: next-through})` and then `require('./data.json')` — no Sentry in the process at all. Deno 2.9.0 -> "json FAILED: SyntaxError Unexpected token ':'"; node v26.5.0 -> "json ok: {"a":1}". Deno 2.8.3 not tested: $S/deno283/deno does not exist on this machine.

D. Why mysql@2 specifically cannot be rescued: it stays in Sentry's `DEFAULT_SERVER_EXTERNAL_PACKAGES` (packages/nextjs/src/config/withSentryConfig/constants.ts:23-24) while `BUNDLE_SAFE_INSTRUMENTED_PACKAGES = ['ioredis']` (packages/nextjs/src/config/diagnosticsChannelInjection.ts:9) is the only list removed from those externals when buildTimeInstrumentation is on. I forced mysql to be bundled anyway (a webpack-externals wrapper in next.config.mjs, BUNDLE_MYSQL=1, distDir .next-bundlemysql). The build-time transform then fires on Deno — `orchestrion:mysql:` is in the chunks and the span appears: transaction "GET /api/dbmysql" spans ["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /api/dbmysql/route","db SELECT id, name FROM users"] — but the driver itself breaks: HTTP 500, "Error: Received packet in the wrong sequence." then "Error: Cannot enqueue l after fatal error." (mangled class name 'l'). Same failure on Node v26.5.0 with the same build (server-node-bundlemysql.log), so this is a mysql-2.x-cannot-be-bundled defect, not a Deno one, and the allowlist is right to exclude it.

Net: on Deno the db-span story is three-way, not two-way. Native-channel drivers work (mysql2 >= 3.11, ioredis >= 5.11). Build-time-instrumented drivers work (today only ioredis < 5.11, via the orchestrion webpack loader — no runtime hook needed). Drivers that stay external and depend on the runtime module hook (mysql 2.x, pg, and everything else in Sentry's serverExternalPackages defaults) record nothing, because `Module.registerHooks` has to be off for Next.js to serve a single request on Deno.

Not tested: pg/mongodb (no server available), Turbopack (`resolveBuildTimeInstrumentationOption` disables build-time instrumentation on Turbopack below Next 16, so it can only be worse), Deno 2.8.3 (binary missing). There is no Next.js-on-Deno e2e app in the repo to use as a reference, and `enableRuntimeChannelInjection` appears nowhere in ~/dev/sentry-docs.
workaround: Next.js on Deno needs `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false` in `Sentry.init()` (sentry.server.config.js) or every request 500s with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`. With that set, db spans still arrive for drivers that do not need the runtime module hook: mysql2 >= 3.11 and ioredis >= 5.11 (own diagnostics_channel), and ioredis < 5.11 (bundled and transformed at build time by `withSentryConfig`'s default `buildTimeInstrumentation`, which requires the webpack builder — do not pass `--turbopack` on Next 15, and do not set `buildTimeInstrumentation: false`). For mysql 2.x / pg there is no workaround: forcing them out of `serverExternalPackages` does produce the span but corrupts the driver on Node as well as Deno.
docsImpact: On Deno, add `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false` to `Sentry.init()` in `sentry.server.config.js` — Deno cannot run the diagnostics-channel module hook (`require()` of a `.json` file throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`, denoland/deno#36240), so Next.js 500s on every request without it; with it, database and other library spans are recorded only for packages that ship their own `diagnostics_channel` (mysql2 >= 3.11, ioredis >= 5.11) or that Sentry instruments at build time (ioredis < 5.11, which needs the default webpack builder and `buildTimeInstrumentation`), while drivers Sentry keeps in `serverExternalPackages` — mysql 2.x, pg — produce no spans on Deno.

details:
Baseline reproduced, then refuted with a one-line addition to `Sentry.init()`.

Probe dir: $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-nextjs-deno-outgoingfetch (node_modules removed; REPRO.md has the exact commands). deno 2.9.0 (stable, release, aarch64-apple-darwin), next@15.5.4, develop tarballs 10.67.0. Ports: sink 41611, recorder 41612, app 41613-41618.

A. BASELINE (the reported wiring: enableRuntimeChannelInjection:false, no fetch integration) — claim reproduced exactly.

  {"url": "/rec", "sentry-trace": null, "baggage": null, "traceparent": null}

sink:
  {"type": "transaction", "name": "GET /api/fetch", "op": "http.server", "source": "route", "status": "ok", "trace_id": "1939cc8124c84062b69e6380a88c8845", "sdk": "sentry.javascript.nextjs", "spans": ["resolve page components", "executing api route (app) /api/fetch/route", "http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41612/rec", "start response"]}
The http.client span's trace_id equals the trace_id in the outgoing sentry-trace header, so distributed tracing out of the server is intact.

C. Same fix under traceLifecycle 'stream' (span envelopes):
  ["resolve page components", "http.client GET 127.0.0.1"]
  ["executing api route (app) /api/fetch/route", "start response", "http.server GET /api/fetch"]
  recorder: sentry-trace "a4f65c5faa5f432b8981a8b1922f9784-8e95e6f588a6096d-1", baggage present.

D. Equivalent hand-rolled integration also verified (sentry-fetch-integration.js): `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest` + `shouldPropagateTraceForUrl` + `isSentryRequestUrl` from `@sentry/core`, spanOrigin 'auto.http.fetch'. Produced the same http.client span and headers under both lifecycles. `tracePropagationTargets` is NOT needed (verified with it removed); the server default propagates everywhere.

Why it works: `@sentry/core`'s `instrumentFetch()` (packages/core/src/instrument/fetch.ts:47) deliberately skips the native-fetch probe outside the browser and always patches `GLOBAL_OBJ.fetch`, so it sees Deno's global fetch and also survives Next.js' own fetch patch. What is missing is only that no runtime SDK reachable from `@sentry/nextjs` on Deno registers such an integration: `@sentry/node` ships only undici/NodeFetch instrumentation, and `@sentry/deno` has no fetch integration at all (`@sentry/bun` and `@sentry/cloudflare` do, in their defaults). So the gap is a missing default, not a runtime limitation.

Unrelated trap worth recording: a failed `next build` leaves a corrupt distDir, and every subsequent build then dies with `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input at .next/server/webpack-runtime.js` while collecting page data. This made a first winterCGFetch attempt look like an incompatibility; it built and ran fine after pointing `distDir` at a fresh directory. Do not conclude "package X breaks the Next build on Deno" without a clean distDir.

Not retested here (out of scope, unchanged): `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false` is still required, otherwise every request 500s.
docsImpact: On Deno, the Node SDK's HTTP client instrumentation only sees `node:http`/undici requests, so calls made with the global `fetch` produce no `http.client` span and carry no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers; add `integrations: [winterCGFetchIntegration()]` from `@sentry/vercel-edge` (already installed with `@sentry/nextjs`) to your `Sentry.init()` to get outgoing-fetch spans and distributed tracing.

details:
Refuted on both halves of the report. Under the DOCUMENTED wiring (`import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt'`, sdk stays `sentry.javascript.nuxt`), Nuxt 4.5.2 on bun 1.4.0 with `NITRO_PRESET=bun` produces fully attributed db spans nested under the request span, and the mysql2 query does NOT have to fail. Two independent, separately provable causes were behind the "partial":

CAUSE 1 - the missing parent span, not missing instrumentation. `@sentry/server-utils` mysql2 subscriber binds its channels with `{ requiresParentSpan: true }` (worktree packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql2/mysql2-dc-subscriber.ts:125 and :144). On bun, `@sentry/nuxt` alone creates no `http.server` span (the h3 patch logs only "Patched h3 event handler. Created new isolation scope."), so every mysql2 span is suppressed. Adding `integrations: [bunServerIntegration()]` (imported from `@sentry/bun`, init still from `@sentry/nuxt`) restores the parent and the db spans appear. Proof that instrumentation was never absent: the `mysql` v2 driver (which the repo's own e2e app nuxt-4/server/api/db-mysql.ts uses) has NO `requiresParentSpan`, and under plain `@sentry/nuxt` on bun it already emitted a complete span - as its own root transaction:
  {"name":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0","info":{"source":"custom"},"trace":{"op":"db","origin":"auto.db.mysql","data":{"db.system.name":"mysql","db.namespace":"app","db.query.text":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0","db.query.summary":"SELECT users","server.address":"127.0.0.1","server.port":3307}}}
That also refutes "the build-time orchestrion pass injected nothing": with a driver that needs injection present, `grep -o "orchestrion:[a-z0-9:._-]*" .output/server/index.mjs` -> `orchestrion:mysql:query`, and the boot log shows `[instrumentation:mysql] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly`. The earlier "injected libraries=[]" was an artifact of the app only using mysql2, which publishes its own channels and needs no injection.

CAUSE 2 - `genFunc$1 is not a function` is a Nitro bundling bug with a one-line fix, not an unfixable blocker. `nitro: { externals: { external: ['mysql2', 'mysql2/promise'] } }` keeps mysql2 out of the rollup bundle; the query then returns rows on the first try (`[warmdb] mysql2 ok`, `{"rows":[{"id":1,"name":"ada"},{"id":2,"name":"linus"}]}`). Confirmed the bug is Nitro's, not bun's or Sentry's: the same unexternalized build on `node-server` under plain node fails the same way, and there it also breaks the `mysql` v2 driver (`TypeError: SqlString.format is not a function`) which bun happens to tolerate.

FINAL WORKING RUN, documented wiring, static lifecycle (variant F, $S/deep/verify4-M-nuxt-bun-dbspans/run-b/app-F.log):
  {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/db","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.nuxt","spans":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?"],"spanDetail":[{"op":"db","desc":"mysql2.pool.connect","origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel","db_ns":"app"},{"op":"db","desc":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?","origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel","db_text":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?","db_summary":"SELECT users","db_ns":"app"}]}
  {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/dbmysql","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.nuxt","spans":["db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0"],"spanDetail":[{"op":"db","desc":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0","origin":"auto.db.mysql","db_text":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0","db_summary":"SELECT users","db_ns":"app"}]}

OTHER TRACE LIFECYCLE - stream (the develop default, variant G, run-b/app-G.log): same result, db spans parented to the Bun.serve segment, low-cardinality names:
  {"type":"span","trace_id":"378df42b...","items":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT users","http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"SELECT users","parent_span_id":"afcc488535e06f05","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel","op":"db","db_text":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?","db_summary":"SELECT users","db_ns":"app"},{"name":"GET","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.bun.serve","op":"http.server"}]}
  {"type":"span","trace_id":"f43c68b5...","items":["db SELECT users","http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"SELECT users","parent_span_id":"b1313fbd37da1d4c","origin":"auto.db.mysql","op":"db","db_text":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0","db_summary":"SELECT users","db_ns":"app"}]}

NEW GOTCHA FOUND (bundler variant E, run-b/app-E.log): on bun, externalizing is driver-dependent. With `external: ['mysql','mysql2','mysql2/promise']`, mysql2 still gets spans (it publishes its own channels and the SDK subscribes eagerly) but `mysql` v2 gets NONE - `{"name":"GET /api/dbmysql","op":"http.server","spans":[]}` - because bun has no require hook ("No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping") and an external module cannot receive the build-time orchestrion injection. So on bun: drivers that publish their own channels (mysql2) must be external; drivers that need Sentry's injection (mysql v2) must stay bundled.

VARIANTS RUN (all `NITRO_PRESET=bun npx nuxt build` + `PORT=51842 bun run .output/server/index.mjs`, sink `PORT=51841 node sink.mjs`, MariaDB 127.0.0.1:3307):

B @sentry/nuxt + externals[mysql2]: both queries succeed; mysql2 spans only under a manual `Sentry.startSpan` parent; mysql v2 orphan root span.
C @sentry/bun + externals[mysql2]: full nesting (the previously reported working variant).
D @sentry/nuxt, no externals, node-server preset under node: both drivers break in the bundle (genFunc$1 / SqlString.format), spans still recorded - proves the bundling bug is Nitro's.
E @sentry/bun + externals[mysql,mysql2]: mysql v2 loses its span (see gotcha).
F @sentry/nuxt + bunServerIntegration() + externals[mysql2], static: works.
G same as F, stream lifecycle: works.

Probe files (rerun after `npm install` per the package.json in app/, node_modules removed to save disk): $S/deep/verify4-M-nuxt-bun-dbspans/app/{nuxt.config.ts,sentry.server.config.ts,server/utils/dbpool.ts,server/utils/dbconn.ts,server/api/{db,dbmysql,dbspan,dbmysqlspan,sentinel}.ts,server/plugins/warmdb.ts}; logs in $S/deep/verify4-M-nuxt-bun-dbspans/run-b/; sink at $S/deep/verify4-M-nuxt-bun-dbspans/sink.mjs. app/ is left in the variant-F/G state. All processes killed.
workaround: Keep the documented `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt'` init and add two things. In sentry.server.config.ts: `import { bunServerIntegration } from '@sentry/bun'` and pass `integrations: [bunServerIntegration()]` to `Sentry.init` - the nitro `bun` preset serves through `Bun.serve`, which the Node-based Nuxt SDK does not instrument, and mysql2 spans are bound with `requiresParentSpan: true` so they are dropped without a request span. In nuxt.config.ts: `nitro: { externals: { external: ['mysql2', 'mysql2/promise'] } }` - bundling mysql2 through Nitro's rollup breaks the driver itself (`genFunc$1 is not a function`, and on node `SqlString.format is not a function` for mysql v2). Do not externalize drivers that rely on Sentry's build-time channel injection (`mysql` v2, and anything else without its own diagnostics channels): on bun there is no runtime require hook, so an external module of that kind is never instrumented.
docsImpact: On the Nuxt guide's Bun/Nitro page: "When you deploy Nuxt with the Nitro `bun` preset, keep `Sentry.init` in `sentry.server.config.ts` importing from `@sentry/nuxt`, add `integrations: [bunServerIntegration()]` from `@sentry/bun` so requests served by `Bun.serve` get a span (database spans such as mysql2's are only recorded inside an active request span), and keep native database drivers out of the server bundle with `nitro: { externals: { external: ['mysql2', 'mysql2/promise'] } }`, since Nitro's rollup bundling breaks those drivers at runtime; do not externalize drivers that have no diagnostics channels of their own (for example `mysql` v2), because Bun cannot install the runtime instrumentation hook and only bundled code receives build-time instrumentation."

VARIANT D - same `@sentry/nuxt` init plus `integrations: [bunServerIntegration()]` from `@sentry/bun` (THE FIX):
  event  trace=12345678901234567890123456789012 parent=1234567890123456 name=GET /api/error msg=nuxt-bun-route-error
  span   trace=12345678901234567890123456789012 parent=1234567890123456 seg=True name=GET /users/:id op=http.server
  span   trace=12345678901234567890123456789012 parent=1234567890123456 seg=True name=GET op=http.server
  event  trace=77e88d5450834c69bae4818d7d3c9b1a parent=None name=None msg=sentinel
Incoming trace continued (trace id AND parent span id), an `http.server` segment span is emitted, the parameterized route name `GET /users/:id` survives (the Nuxt route detector sets source=route, so streaming keeps the route in the name), isolation is restored (sentinel gets its own trace), and the SDK identity stays `sentry.javascript.nuxt` - unlike the previously reported workaround of initializing `@sentry/bun`, which reports `sentry.javascript.bun` and drops the Nuxt event processors. Boot log shows `Integration installed: BunServer` next to the normal Node integrations; no conflict with the (inert) `Http` integration.

ROOT CAUSE (verified, not theory): on develop `@sentry/node`'s request isolation, trace continuation and server span all hang off one diagnostics channel - `packages/core/src/integrations/http/constants.ts:3` `HTTP_ON_SERVER_REQUEST = 'http.server.request.start'`, subscribed in `packages/node/src/integrations/http/httpServerIntegration.ts:146`. Bun 1.4.0 never publishes that channel. Direct probe (`dc-probe.mjs`, subscribe + `node:http` server + one fetch):
  bun  -> channel fired: 0
  node -> channel fired: 1
So this is preset-independent: the `bun` preset serves via `Bun.serve` (no `node:http` at all), and even the `node-server` preset run under bun gets no event, which is why the boot log also prints `No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping`. `@sentry/bun` continues the trace because `bunServerIntegration` patches `Bun.serve` and calls `continueTrace` itself (`packages/bun/src/integrations/bunserver.ts:243`). `bunServerIntegration` only depends on `@sentry/core` APIs, which is why dropping it into a Nuxt/Node client works.

workaround:
Keep the documented `@sentry/nuxt` wiring and add the Bun server integration to it. `sentry.server.config.ts`:

  import { bunServerIntegration } from '@sentry/bun'
  import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt'

  Sentry.init({
    dsn: '...',
    tracesSampleRate: 1.0,
    integrations: [bunServerIntegration()],
  })

Requires `@sentry/bun` as a dependency (Nitro bundles it into `.output/server/node_modules`) and `sentry: { autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import' }` in `nuxt.config.ts`, because bun ignores NODE_OPTIONS and has no `--import` flag. Build with `NITRO_PRESET=bun npx nuxt build`, run with `bun run .output/server/index.mjs`. This restores incoming trace continuation, `http.server` spans, parameterized route names and request isolation, while events keep `sdk: sentry.javascript.nuxt`. Switching the whole init to `@sentry/bun` also works but loses the Nuxt SDK identity and event processors.
docsImpact: The Nuxt guide (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/, no file mentions bun; index.mdx:61-68 documents only `node --import ./.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs`) needs a Bun section saying: "Running a Nuxt server on Bun: set `sentry.autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import'` (Bun ignores NODE_OPTIONS and has no `--import` flag), build with `NITRO_PRESET=bun`, and add `integrations: [bunServerIntegration()]` from `@sentry/bun` to your `Sentry.init` in `sentry.server.config.ts` - without it Bun's server receives no `http.server.request.start` diagnostics-channel event, so incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers are ignored, no server spans are recorded and requests share one isolation scope."

workaround:
In `sentry.server.config.ts`, install `@sentry/bun` alongside `@sentry/nuxt` and pass its Bun.serve integration:

  import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt'

  Sentry.init({
    dsn: '...',
    tracesSampleRate: 1.0,
    integrations: [bunServerIntegration()],
  })

Build with `NITRO_PRESET=bun npx nuxt build` and `sentry: { autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import' }` (bun ignores NODE_OPTIONS and has no `--import`, so the documented `node --import ./.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs` path is unavailable). Run with `bun run .output/server/index.mjs`. This restores per-request trace ids, stops the stale transaction name leaking across requests, and additionally turns on route-named `http.server` spans, while keeping the `sentry.javascript.nuxt` SDK and all Nuxt-specific instrumentation. Replacing the init with `@sentry/bun` entirely also works but gives up the Nuxt SDK identity.
docsImpact: On the Nuxt install pages (`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/install/limited-server-tracing.mdx` and `install/index.mdx`, which currently never mention bun), add: "Running a Nuxt server on Bun (`NITRO_PRESET=bun`) requires `autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import'` — Bun ignores `NODE_OPTIONS` and has no `--import` flag — and additionally requires installing `@sentry/bun` and passing `integrations: [bunServerIntegration()]` to `Sentry.init` in `sentry.server.config.ts`; without it the server runs on `Bun.serve`, which no instrumentation touches, so every event in the process shares one trace id, carries the transaction name of an unrelated earlier request, and no server spans are recorded."

details:
REFUTED. Both halves of the claim are wrong. (1) "No instrumentation path exists / injected nothing." The @sentry/nuxt build-time bundler plugin DOES instrument mysql2 inside the nitro rollup bundle, even for `deno_server`. Proof from the built output (no runtime hook involved, mysql2 is fully bundled): $ grep -oE "tracingChannel\('[^']+'\)" .output/server/chunks/_/db.mjs | sort -u tracingChannel('mysql2:connect') tracingChannel('mysql2:execute') tracingChannel('mysql2:pool:connect') tracingChannel('mysql2:query') The runtime debug lines `[Sentry] Bundler plugin ran, injected libraries=[]` and `[Sentry] Runtime hook registered, injected libraries=[]` are MISLEADING: the bundler list is populated at build time in a different process and is always empty at runtime. The prior agent read those lines as the verdict; the bundle contradicts them. The app log also shows the channel integrations do subscribe on Deno: `[instrumentation:mysql2] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly`. (2) "genFunc$1 is not a function / no db span reachable." Fixed by one nitro option, already present in the app under test: nitro: { preset: 'deno_server', externals: { inline: ['generate-function', 'named-placeholders'] } } With that, /api/db returns 200 with real rows from MariaDB. Sink evidence, deno_server preset, traceLifecycle 'static' (port 41352): {"type":"transaction","name":"manual-parent","op":"manual","source":"custom","status":"ok", "sdk":"sentry.javascript.nuxt","spans":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} Same app, default lifecycle (stream, traceLifecycle line removed), port 41353: {"type":"span","trace_id":"025c66c6...","items":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT users","manual manual-parent"], "raw":[{"name":"SELECT users","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"b50b3bcbcacf1bb1","is_segment":false, "origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel"}, ...]} Low-cardinality name and correct origin, so the spans are genuine auto-instrumentation, not something the probe faked. The one real limit on `deno_server`: the db subscriber is registered with `requiresParentSpan: true` (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql2/mysql2-dc-subscriber.ts:125 and :146), and the `deno_server` output serves via `Deno.serve`, not `node:http`, so no `http.server` span exists to be that parent. A bare `/api/db` therefore returns 200 with zero span envelopes; only a handler wrapped in `Sentry.startSpan` gets db spans. Confirmed in the app log: for `/api/db` there is only `Patched h3 event handler. Using existing isolation scope.` and no `[Tracing] Starting sampled span`. workaround:
Two things, both one line.

1. Make mysql2 runnable in the nitro bundle (fixes `genFunc$1 is not a function`), in nuxt.config.ts:
   nitro: { externals: { inline: ['generate-function', 'named-placeholders'] } }

2. Prefer `nitro: { preset: 'node-server' }` (or `NITRO_PRESET=node-server`) and run the output with `deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env --allow-sys --allow-ffi --unstable-byonm --unstable-detect-cjs ./server/index.mjs`. Deno is still the runtime, but nitro serves over `node:http`, so you get `http.server` root spans, per-request traces, request data — and therefore db spans on ordinary route handlers with no code change. The SDK also injects `import './sentry.server.config.mjs';` into `.output/server/index.mjs` correctly with this preset.

If you must keep `preset: 'deno_server'`: db spans still work, but only inside an explicit `Sentry.startSpan(...)` in the handler, because `Deno.serve` produces no request span to parent them. You must also create the entry wrapper yourself, since the module writes the config import into a file named `.output/server/deno.json start`:
   printf "import './sentry.server.config.mjs';\nimport './index.mjs';\n" > .output/server/boot.mjs
   cd .output && deno run ... ./server/boot.mjs
docsImpact: On the Nuxt guide's Deno/nitro page: "Database, AI and other library spans are instrumented at build time by the Sentry Nuxt module, so they work on Deno. Two things are required: add `nitro: { externals: { inline: ['generate-function', 'named-placeholders'] } }` to `nuxt.config.ts` so mysql2's `generate-function` dependency survives nitro's rollup bundling, and use the `node-server` preset rather than `deno_server` — you still run the output with `deno run`, but nitro then serves over `node:http`, which is what gives you `http.server` request spans; with `deno_server` the app is served by `Deno.serve`, no request span is created, and database spans (which are only recorded when a parent span is active) never appear unless you wrap the handler in `Sentry.startSpan()` yourself. Note also that with `autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import'` and the `deno_server` preset the module writes the config import into a file named `.output/server/deno.json start` instead of the entry, so you must create your own wrapper entry that imports `./sentry.server.config.mjs` before `./index.mjs`. The runtime debug lines `[Sentry] Bundler plugin ran, injected libraries=[]` do not mean instrumentation is missing; that list is only populated during the build."

Headers work, spans only partly: the `http.client` child of an explicit `Sentry.startSpan` is emitted ({"type":"transaction","name":"manual-root-fetch",...,"spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:28842/rec-inspan"]}), but the three parentless ones are dropped: `Sentry Logger [log]: Sending outcomes: [ { reason: "no_parent_span", category: "span", quantity: 3 } ]`. Root cause: nothing in the Node-side default integration set instruments a non-undici global `fetch`. `nativeNodeFetchIntegration` (`packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/index.ts`) only subscribes to undici diagnostics channels, which Deno's Rust-native `fetch` never emits, and `@sentry/deno`'s own default set (`packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:29-47`: denoServe, denoHttp, breadcrumbs, ...) has no global-fetch integration either. So this is a missing integration, not a runtime limitation, and finding K2 is fixable in the SDK.

Two real defects seen along the way, both narrower than the reported one:
1. `addSentryTopImport` writes the import into a file literally named `.output-deno2/server/deno.json start` (46 bytes: the import line plus the string "undefined"). Cause is `getFilenameFromNodeStartCommand` parsing Nitro's deno preset preview command `deno task --config .output-deno2/deno.json start` (packages/nuxt/src/vite/addServerConfig.ts:92-104); it takes the token after `--config` and the trailing `start` word. 2. Route-name enrichment does not run on error responses, on Deno AND on Node alike: `/api/users/boom` yields `"name":"GET /api/users/boom","source":"url"`. Nitro v2 goes through `update-route-name-legacy.server.ts` (`beforeResponse` hook), which is not invoked for a thrown handler. Not runtime-specific, so it belongs to a separate finding.
workaround: Do not set `nitro: { preset: 'deno_server' }`. Build the default `node-server` output (`npx nuxt build`) and run it with Deno: `cd .output/server && deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env --allow-sys --allow-ffi --unstable-byonm ./index.mjs`. Nitro's node-server entry uses `node:http`, which Deno's Node compat layer serves and which @sentry/node instruments, so `http.server` spans, `getActiveSpan()` inside handlers, and the `updateRouteBeforeResponse` hook (parameterized `GET /api/users/:id`, `source: "route"`, `url.path.parameter.*`) all work. Both `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and the default `'stream'` produce the parameterized name. If the `deno_server` preset is required for other reasons, there is no workaround for route names, and the sentry import must additionally be prepended to `.output/server/index.mjs` by hand.

details:
Could NOT refute the "partial" report. Out of the box, with `Bun.serve({ fetch: req => app.fetch(req) })`, the server span carries no route. Reproduced in both lifecycles and in a bundle; the only thing that changes it is user code at the mount, not SDK config.

Root cause read from the SDK source, not guessed: `~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/packages/bun/src/integrations/bunserver.ts:194-224` — `wrapRequestHandler(..., route?)` sets `SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE='route'` + `url.template` only when a `route` string is passed, and the only caller that passes one is `instrumentBunServeRoutes` iterating `serveOptions.routes` (line 127-176). No `routes` map means `routeName = parsedUrl.pathname` and source `url`. Nothing in the SDK reads an Oak/Koa-style router.

Variants I ran (all against my own sink on 127.0.0.1:53197, app ports 54101-54119):

1) Baseline, `fetch: req => app.fetch(req)`, stream:
   SPAN name=GET op=http.server status=ok src=url tmpl=-
   SPAN name=GET op=http.server status=error src=url tmpl=-
   SPAN name=SELECT users op=db status=ok src=- tmpl=-
2) Baseline, static:
   TX name=GET /users/7 source=url status=ok tmpl=-
   TX name=GET /error source=url status=internal_error tmpl=-
   (Note a correction to the original report: static does NOT give a bare `GET`; it gives the raw pathname with source=url, i.e. a high-cardinality name.)
3) Bundled with `@sentry/bun/plugin` (`Bun.build({ target:'bun', external:['@sentry/*'], plugins:[sentryBunPlugin()] })`, then `bun dist/app.js`) — identical to baseline:
   === BUNDLED MODE=fetch
   SPAN name=GET op=http.server src=url  (x5; db span present, so the plugin did work, it just does not know Oak)
4) Init placement (import "./instrument" first line vs `--preload`) and `traceLifecycle` make no difference to the source attribute.
5) `app.listen({ port })` mount: server spans DO arrive (contradicting "effectively unsupported"), but method-only and with no request context:
   {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"GET","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.bun.serve"}]}  (x5, /error one has status error)
   The naming middleware logs `[naming] /users/7 span=false route=/users/:id` for every request — `getActiveSpan()` is undefined inside Oak middleware under listen — and the thrown error produced no event and `/db` produced no db span. So under listen the spans exist but are unnameable and context-free.

BETTER WORKAROUND THAN THE ONE REPORTED (this is the one thing I would change in the finding). Instead of a per-request Sentry middleware, derive Bun's `routes` map from the Oak router at mount time. It contains zero Sentry API, runs once, and makes the SDK's own route naming fire:

  const handler = (req: Request) => app.fetch(req);
  const routes: Record<string, typeof handler> = {};
  for (const r of router) routes[r.path] = handler;
  Bun.serve({ port, hostname: "127.0.0.1", routes, fetch: handler });

  === MODE=derived LIFECYCLE=stream
  SPAN name=GET /users/:id op=http.server status=ok src=route tmpl=/users/:id
  SPAN name=GET /db op=http.server status=ok src=route tmpl=/db
  SPAN name=GET /error op=http.server status=error src=route tmpl=/error
  === MODE=derived LIFECYCLE=static
  TX name=GET /users/:id source=route status=ok tmpl=/users/:id
  TX name=GET /error source=route status=internal_error tmpl=/error
  {"exception":"Error: oak bun boom","mechanism":"auto.http.bun.serve","handled":false}
  Same result bundled. It also sets `url.template`, which the reported middleware does not.

Limits of that workaround, measured with Oak's exotic path shapes (tricky.ts): `Bun.serve` accepts them without throwing, and anything it does not match falls through to the `fetch` handler, so behavior is never changed, only the name. `/api/opt` (matching `/api/opt/:a?`) and `/api/star/a/b` (matching `/api/star/(.*)`) fell through and got `SPAN name=GET ... src=url`. And Bun ignores an inline regex constraint, so `/api/num/abc` — which Oak 404s — was still labeled `SPAN name=GET /api/num/:id(\d+) status=error src=route`. Plain and `:param` routes are exact.

Repo reference: the only Bun e2e app, `~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/bun-mysql/src/app.ts`, mounts a bare `fetch(req)` with manual `url.pathname` branching, so the repo itself has no example of route-named Bun spans and no Oak app at all.

workaround: Give Bun.serve a `routes` map derived from the Oak router at startup, and keep `fetch` as the fallback: `const handler = (req: Request) => app.fetch(req); const routes: Record<string, typeof handler> = {}; for (const r of router) routes[r.path] = handler; Bun.serve({ port, routes, fetch: handler });`. This yields `GET /users/:id` with `sentry.segment.name.source=route` and `url.template` in both stream and static lifecycles, on the error path too, bundled or not, with no Sentry-specific code. Routes using regex constraints, optional params or `(.*)` are named imprecisely or fall back to the method-only name; list those explicitly in the map if their names matter. The alternative is the reported router-level middleware (`Sentry.updateSpanName` + `SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE`), which also works but runs per request and does not set `url.template`. Neither works under `app.listen()`.
docsImpact: On Bun, Sentry names the server span from the `routes` map you pass to `Bun.serve`, so an Oak app mounted as `Bun.serve({ fetch: req => app.fetch(req) })` produces spans named `GET` (source `url`) no matter the lifecycle, init placement, or whether you bundle with `@sentry/bun/plugin`; to get route names, build the `routes` map from your router at startup — `const handler = (req: Request) => app.fetch(req); const routes = {}; for (const r of router) routes[r.path] = handler; Bun.serve({ port, routes, fetch: handler });` — which yields `GET /users/:id` with `sentry.segment.name.source=route` and `url.template` on success and error paths alike (routes with regex constraints, optional params or wildcards fall back to the method-only name), and note that `app.listen()` must not be used: its spans arrive method-named and Oak middleware sees no active span, so errors and database spans inside a request are lost.

Oak has no Sentry integration, so `withSentry` alone names the request span after the raw URL (`GET /users/42`, source `url`) with `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and after the method alone (`GET`) with the default `'stream'`; to get parameterized names, register one Oak middleware before `router.routes()` that reads `ctx.matched` inside a `try/finally` (so it also runs when a handler throws) and calls `Sentry.updateSpanName(Sentry.getRootSpan(span), routeName)`, `rootSpan.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, 'route')` — the exported constant, not the string `'sentry.source'`, which the SDK ignores — plus `Sentry.getIsolationScope().setTransactionName(routeName)` so error events carry the route too.
