capability: db spans (mysql2) on React Router 8 framework mode, custom Express/node:http server, @sentry/react-router 10.67.0 (develop), bun 1.4.0
details:
REFUTED. db spans do work on Bun with @sentry/react-router 10.67.0 once two Bun-specific gaps are closed. Both are real defects, neither is documented, and neither has anything to do with orchestrion injection - the reporter's diagnosis was a false lead (the `orchestrion:mysql2:query`/`:execute` strings they found in `build/server/assets/context-*.js` are just the channel-name constants inside the bundled `@sentry/server-utils` config, not injected publishers; mysql2 3.24.3 is >= 3.20 so the SDK config marks it `registrationOnly` and relies on mysql2's own NATIVE `mysql2:query` / `mysql2:execute` / `mysql2:connect` / `mysql2:pool:connect` diagnostics channels, no code transform involved). PROBE DIR: $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-reactrouter-bun-dbspans/ (app/ = scaffolded `node-custom-server` template, React Router 8 + Express 5 + vite 8; logs `run-*.log`, `app-*.log`). BASELINE (reproduces the report), `PORT=47312 bun server.js`, no changes: 
{"rows":[{"id":1,"name":"ada"}],"count":2,"activeSpan":false}
sink: only `{"type":"event","message":"sentinel"}` - no transaction, no span envelope, no db span. FIX (both parts needed), `app/instrument.server.mjs`: import * as Sentry from "@sentry/react-router"; import { bunHttpServerIntegration } from "@sentry/bun"; Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: "static", integrations: [bunHttpServerIntegration()] }); await import("mysql2/promise"); // Bun: keep the diagnostics channels alive Then `PORT=47341 bun server.js` (stock `server.js` with `import "./instrument.server.mjs"` as line 1): transaction GET /users/:id src=route | ["middleware ","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?","db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT name FROM users"] Stable over a 30s soak, 6 requests spaced 5s apart, every one carried the db spans (run-soak30.log). Also works with `traceLifecycle: 'stream'`: span ["db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users","db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT users","http.server GET /users/:id","middleware "] DEFECT A - no root span on Bun for node:http servers. Bun does not publish Node's `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel, which `@sentry/node`'s `httpServerIntegration` subscribes to (packages/node/src/integrations/http/httpServerIntegration.ts:146). Proof (micro/httpdc.mjs): node prints `DC http.server.request.start FIRED`, bun prints only `status 200`. All db subscribers are registered with `{ requiresParentSpan: true }` (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql2/index.ts:110 and mysql2-dc-subscriber), so with no request span there is no db span either. `@sentry/bun`'s `bunHttpServerIntegration()` exists exactly for this (it patches `http.Server.prototype.emit` and hands the server to the same core instrumentation) but `@sentry/react-router` neither ships nor mentions it. A hand-rolled Express middleware that opens a `forceTransaction` span around `next()` works equally well (`ROOT_SPAN_MIDDLEWARE=1` in app/server.js). DEFECT B - Bun garbage-collects diagnostics-channel bindings. Bun's `node:diagnostics_channel` holds channels weakly and drops subscribers/bound stores once the caller releases its reference; Node keeps them. Proof (micro/gc.mjs): --- node: immediately: dropped= true kept= true sub= true / after gc: dropped= true kept= true sub= true --- bun: immediately: dropped= true kept= true sub= true / after gc: dropped= false kept= true sub= false The SDK discards the `TracingChannelBindingHandle` returned by `bindTracingChannelToSpan`, so on Bun every channel-based integration silently dies at the first GC. Directly visible with only the SDK loaded (micro/sdkbind.mjs, `Sentry.init` then read `tracingChannel('mysql2:query').start.hasSubscribers`): --- node: [sync] true ... [after 50ms] mysql2:query start.hasSubscribers= true --- bun: [sync] true ... [after 50ms] mysql2:query start.hasSubscribers= false Consequence inside the app: with the root span present but nothing holding the channels, mysql2's own `shouldTrace()` gate reads `channel.hasSubscribers ?? channel.start?.hasSubscribers` (undefined on Bun, then false) and never publishes: [route] dcState {"startHasSubscribers":false} <- inside the RR server bundle, bun [route] dcState {"hasSubscribers":true,"startHasSubscribers":true} <- same build, node sink, bun, root span but no keepalive: transaction GET /users/:id | ["middleware "] sink, bun, root span + keepalive: transaction GET /users/:id | [... ,"db SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", ...] Any strong reference fixes it: `await import("mysql2/promise")` in the instrument file (mysql2 caches the channels at module scope), or `globalThis.x = ['mysql2:query','mysql2:execute','mysql2:connect','mysql2:pool:connect'].map(tracingChannel)`. Both were measured working after a 12s soak. CONTROL - the exact same `react-router build` output under node (`PORT=47317 node server.js`, no workarounds) emits db spans out of the box: transaction GET /users/:id | ["middleware compression","middleware logger","middleware serveStatic","middleware mounted_app","middleware ","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?","db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT name FROM users"] So the Vite/`sentryReactRouter` build is fine; only the Bun runtime path is broken. Confirmed side notes: the reporter's `entry.server.tsx` rewrite to `renderToReadableStream` + `Sentry.wrapSentryHandleRequest` is indeed required on Bun (`react-dom/server` resolves to `server.bun.js`, no `renderToPipeableStream`), and `ssr.noExternal: ["mysql2"]` is unnecessary - `sentryOrchestrionPlugin`'s own `config` hook already force-bundles every instrumented module. NOT RUN: the CI pin bun 1.3.14 - `$S/bun1314/` does not exist on this machine (only `deep`, `pack`, `qs` and three html files are under `$S`). All results are bun 1.4.0 and node v26.5.0. Reproduce: `cd .../verify4-M-reactrouter-bun-dbspans/app && npm install && npm install $S/pack/sentry-{react-router,node,core,browser,react,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry,bundler-plugins,browser-utils,replay,replay-canvas,feedback,bun}-10.67.0.tgz mysql2 && npx react-router build`, start `PORT=47311 node $S/qs/sink.mjs`, then `PORT= BUN_HTTP=1 KEEPALIVE=driver SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:47311/ bun server.js`. `app/micro/{httpdc,gc,sdkbind,tcid,bindstore}.mjs` are the standalone one-file proofs of each mechanism.
workaround: In `instrument.server.mjs`, add `integrations: [bunHttpServerIntegration()]` from `@sentry/bun` to the `@sentry/react-router` `Sentry.init()` call (Bun never publishes Node's `http.server.request.start` channel, so without it there is no request span and db spans are suppressed by `requiresParentSpan`), and immediately after `Sentry.init()` add `await import("mysql2/promise")` so a module-scope reference keeps the mysql2 diagnostics channels alive against Bun's weak channel registry. Both are needed; either alone yields zero db spans. Equivalent alternatives: a `forceTransaction` Express middleware instead of `bunHttpServerIntegration()`, and `globalThis.__keep = ['mysql2:query','mysql2:execute','mysql2:connect','mysql2:pool:connect'].map(n => tracingChannel(n))` instead of the driver import.
docsImpact: On Bun, the React Router server SDK needs two extra lines in the instrumentation file: add `bunHttpServerIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` to `Sentry.init()` (Bun does not emit the `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel, so without it no request span is created and database, cache and other child spans are dropped), and import your database driver (for example `await import("mysql2/promise")`) right after `Sentry.init()` so its diagnostics channels are not garbage-collected by Bun's weak channel registry.

capability: incoming trace (React Router 8 framework mode, custom Express/Node server, @sentry/react-router 10.67.0 develop, bun 1.4.0)
details:
REFUTED. The capability works once one integration is added to `Sentry.init()`.

Root cause of the original finding: trace continuation for incoming requests lives in core's `instrumentServer()` (packages/core/src/integrations/http/server-subscription.ts:174-215), which clones the isolation scope and calls `continueTrace({ sentryTrace, baggage })` around the server's `emit('request')`. On Node that function is reached through the `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel, subscribed by `httpServerIntegration` (packages/node/src/integrations/http/httpServerIntegration.ts:145-147). Bun never publishes that channel, and it is NOT a native Node channel either, so nothing feeds the server in. Confirmed empirically:

  $ bun chantest.mjs   # subscribe to http.server.request.start + fire a node:http request
  CHANNELS_FIRED=[]
  $ node chantest.mjs
  CHANNELS_FIRED=[]

The SDK already ships the Bun-side bridge: `bunHttpServerIntegration()` (packages/bun/src/integrations/bunHttpServer.ts) patches `http.Server.prototype.emit` and hands each server to the very same `getHttpServerSubscriptions` → `instrumentServer` path. It is a DEFAULT integration of `@sentry/bun`'s own `init()` (packages/bun/src/sdk.ts:72), but `@sentry/react-router` inits through `@sentry/node`'s defaults, so on Bun it is simply absent.

BASELINE (reproduces the report exactly) — `instrument.server.mjs` with the stock `Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' })`, request to `/users/1?mode=error` carrying `sentry-trace: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` + matching baggage, then `/flush`:

  {"type":"event","exception":"Error: loader boom on bun","transaction":"GET /users/:id","trace_id":"0671c2fefd714012926c8459b88db3f9","parent_span_id":"818e49cea0649f2b","dsc_trace_id":"0671c2fefd714012926c8459b88db3f9"}
  {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","trace_id":"0671c2fefd714012926c8459b88db3f9"}          <- no parent_span_id at all
  {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","transaction":"GET /flush","trace_id":"0671c2fefd714012926c8459b88db3f9"}   <- same process-wide trace, no isolation

AFTER adding the integration (the ONLY change; nothing else touched):

  import * as Sentry from '@sentry/react-router';
  import { bunHttpServerIntegration } from '@sentry/bun';
  Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static',
                integrations: [bunHttpServerIntegration()] });

Same two requests:

  {"type":"event","exception":"Error: loader boom on bun","transaction":"GET /users/:id","trace_id":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","span_id":"8bdb7086bcb60330","parent_span_id":"85ceb6a4360ac28b","dsc_trace_id":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","dsc_sampled":"true","user":{"ip_address":"::ffff:127.0.0.1"},"request":{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:47313/users/1?mode=error","method":"GET","headers":{"sentry-trace":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1","baggage":"..."}}}
  {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","parent_span_id":"bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb","spans":["function /users/:id"]}
  {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","transaction":"GET /flush","trace_id":"8d1ca89e0e5e42389749a0ff61121f40"}   <- separate trace: isolation restored

So: trace_id == the incoming aaaa… id, the segment's parent_span_id == the incoming bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb, DSC propagated, request/IP data attached, and per-request isolation works. Three bonus effects fall out of the same change: request isolation, `request` data on events, and an `http.server` root span.

Also verified with the DEVELOP DEFAULT lifecycle `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` (span envelopes):

  {"type":"span","trace_id":"eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee","items":["function /users/:id","http.server GET /users/:id"],
   "raw":[{"name":"/users/:id","status":"error","parent_span_id":"866761be6b58c7bf","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.function.react_router.instrumentation_api"},
          {"name":"GET /users/:id","status":"error","parent_span_id":"2222222222222222","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.react_router.instrumentation_api"}]}

and the error event on that request carried trace_id `eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee`.

Independence check — the fix is NOT an artifact of React Router 8's instrumentation API (`Sentry.createSentryServerInstrumentation()`). A plain Express route registered in `server.js` that never reaches the React Router handler continues the trace too, and two different incoming traces stay separate:

  event Error: plain express boom trace= cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc parent= 1111111111111111
  transaction GET /plain           trace= cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc parent= 1111111111111111
  event Error: plain express boom trace= dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd parent= 1111111111111111
  transaction GET /plain           trace= dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd parent= 1111111111111111
  event sentinel                   trace= 2bd7655b22e14a0f9be917010461eb04

Notes / caveats:
- `@sentry/bun` must be installed alongside `@sentry/react-router` and must dedupe to ONE `@sentry/core@10.67.0` (verified: only `node_modules/@sentry/core` exists, no nested copy). Installed with `npm install $S/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz $S/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $S/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $S/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz $S/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $S/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz`.
- The debug warning "No diagnostics-channel injection detected. Channel-based integrations will not record spans." is still printed and is still accurate for *library* spans (express/db/AI) — those remain absent without a Bun bundle. It is misleading here in that incoming-request tracing is fully fixed while the warning still fires.
- The Bun workaround the original probe found is still required: `app/entry.server.tsx` must use `renderToReadableStream`, because Bun resolves `react-dom/server` to `server.bun.js` which has no `renderToPipeableStream`. That means `Sentry.createSentryHandleRequest(...)` (the wiring the docs and the `react-router-8-framework` e2e app show) is unusable on Bun; `Sentry.wrapSentryHandleRequest(handler)` is.
- bun 1.3.14 (the CI pin) could NOT be cross-checked: `$S/bun1314` no longer exists on this machine. Only bun 1.4.0 was tested.
- The repo's own reference app `~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/react-router-8-framework` runs Node with `NODE_OPTIONS='--import ./instrument.mjs'`, which is exactly the mechanism Bun lacks.

docsImpact: On the React Router (and any `@sentry/node`-based framework) guide, add a Bun section: "When you run the server with `bun` instead of `node`, Bun does not emit the `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel the Node SDK relies on, so incoming requests get no isolation scope and no trace continuation from `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers. Install `@sentry/bun` at the same version and add `integrations: [bunHttpServerIntegration()]` to your server-side `Sentry.init()`. Note also that Bun resolves `react-dom/server` to a build without `renderToPipeableStream`, so use `renderToReadableStream` in `app/entry.server.tsx` and wrap it with `Sentry.wrapSentryHandleRequest()` rather than `Sentry.createSentryHandleRequest()`."

On Bun, `node:http` never emits the `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel that the Node-based SDKs use to isolate each incoming request, so any Bun server built on `node:http` (Express, React Router framework mode with a custom server, Next.js) must add `bunHttpServerIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` to `Sentry.init` — without it every request shares one isolation scope and one trace, so `setTag`/`setUser` from one request leak into every other request's events, and no `http.server` spans are recorded.

capability: outgoing fetch (React Router 8 framework mode, custom Express server, @sentry/react-router 10.67.0 develop, bun 1.4.0)
details:
REFUTED. The default `@sentry/react-router` init on Bun really does nothing for outgoing fetch (the report is right about the default), but one added integration fixes it completely, no bundler and no code change in the loader.

EXACT CHANGE, in `instrument.server.mjs`:

  import * as Sentry from "@sentry/react-router";
  import { fetchIntegration, bunHttpServerIntegration } from "@sentry/bun";

  Sentry.init({
    dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0,
    integrations: process.versions.bun ? [fetchIntegration(), bunHttpServerIntegration()] : [],
  });

plus `@sentry/bun@10.67.0` in the install line (`$S/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz`). `fetchIntegration()` alone is enough for the capability under test; `bunHttpServerIntegration()` additionally supplies the incoming-request span and per-request isolation that the report also found missing.

Why the default fails: `nativeNodeFetchIntegration` (packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/index.ts) calls `instrumentUndici()`, which is undici-diagnostics-channel based; Bun implements no such channel, hence the `No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks` warning. `@sentry/bun`'s `fetchIntegration` (packages/bun/src/integrations/fetch.ts) instead wraps global `fetch` via core's `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest`, which works on Bun. It is a plain `defineIntegration` over `@sentry/core` primitives, so it composes with a `@sentry/react-router` client with no dual-core problem (npm dedupes both to one `@sentry/core` 10.67.0).

EVIDENCE (my rerun, sink on 51431, recorder on 51432, app on 51433, `bun 1.4.0 server.js`).

1. baseline (report's setup), static — no span, no headers:
  items: [{"type":"event","message":"sentinel",...}]
  REC /rec {"connection":"keep-alive","user-agent":"Bun/1.4.0","accept":"*/*","host":"127.0.0.1:51432","accept-encoding":"gzip, deflate, br, zstd"}

2. + fetchIntegration(), traceLifecycle 'stream' — span AND headers:
  items: [{"type":"span","trace_id":"8fb773dbbd4d450d9532a39ffbe6fe54","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1"],"raw":[{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.fetch"}]}, {"type":"event","message":"sentinel",...}]
  REC /rec {"baggage":"sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=abc123,sentry-trace_id=8fb773dbbd4d450d9532a39ffbe6fe54,sentry-transaction=GET%20127.0.0.1,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rand=0.478...,sentry-sample_rate=1","sentry-trace":"8fb773dbbd4d450d9532a39ffbe6fe54-a409a1f092ee2976-1",...}

3. + fetchIntegration() + bunHttpServerIntegration(), 'stream' — client span parented under the route-named server span, and per-request isolation (sentinel gets its own trace + `transaction: GET /flush` + request data):
  [{"type":"span","trace_id":"927da38c3b154c39938da5073bab6cda","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","http.server GET /fetchout"],"raw":[{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"80f9adff73b09c45","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.http.fetch"},{"name":"GET /fetchout","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.react_router.request_handler"}]},{"type":"event","message":"sentinel",...,"transaction":"GET /flush","trace_id":"51f55bc88fc9478e894d3313e965aab3","user":{"ip_address":"::ffff:127.0.0.1"},"request":{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:51433/flush",...}}]

4. Same, traceLifecycle 'static' — a normal transaction with the fetch as a child:
  [{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /fetchout","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"c64e46c5090e46f985e09469d02f9734","sdk":"sentry.javascript.react-router","spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:51432/rec"]}, ..., {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /flush",...,"spans":[]}]

TRACE-LIFECYCLE CAVEAT: with `fetchIntegration()` but WITHOUT `bunHttpServerIntegration()`, `traceLifecycle: 'static'` still sends the headers but delivers no span envelope, only a `client_report` (a standalone `http.client` root span is dropped in the static lifecycle):
  items-bunfetch-static: [{"type":"client_report"},{"type":"event","message":"sentinel",...}]
  REC /rec {"baggage":"...sentry-trace_id=4c58fd9d1c2442a186a1d0ed1f0c597c","sentry-trace":"4c58fd9d1c2442a186a1d0ed1f0c597c-9fb6339912a064e5",...}
So on Bun with the static lifecycle you need both integrations, or the stream default.

NODE CAVEAT (why the gate matters): running the identical build under `node` with `fetchIntegration()` unconditionally produces TWO client spans for one fetch:

On Deno, the Node-based SDKs (@sentry/react-router and anything else built on @sentry/node) do not instrument the global `fetch`: Deno's `fetch` is not undici, so it emits none of the diagnostics channels the NodeFetch integration listens on, and outgoing requests made with it get no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers even with `nativeNodeFetchIntegration({ spans: true })` set explicitly — use `node:http`, or import `fetch` from the `undici` package (both are instrumented normally), or register a fetch integration built on `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest` from `@sentry/core`.

[]), 'express']; } }` — and (2) add, as the first express middleware, a hand-written replacement for the monkeypatch the bundle defeats: `app.use((req, res, next) => { Sentry.withIsolationScope(scope => { scope.setSDKProcessingMetadata({ normalizedRequest: { url: `${req.protocol}://${req.get('host')}${req.originalUrl}`, method: req.method, headers: req.headers } }); return Sentry.continueTrace({ sentryTrace: req.headers['sentry-trace'] || '', baggage: req.headers.baggage || '' }, () => next()); }); });`. A Bun guide for Remix v2 must say: `bun server.mjs` gives you errors and logs but no transactions or spans at all, because Sentry's library instrumentation on Bun is build-time only — to get route-named `http.server` transactions (`GET users/:id`) and `LOADER` spans you must bundle the server entry with `Bun.build({ target: 'bun', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` and run the bundle; and because bundling makes Remix's own `createRequestHandler` patch miss, add a `Sentry.withIsolationScope` + `Sentry.continueTrace` wrapper around the Remix express handler in that entry, otherwise every request shares one trace and scope data leaks between requests.

(b) If you must keep the docs-verbatim `@sentry/remix` specifier, force the worker condition ahead of browser in vite.config.ts: `ssr: { target: 'webworker', resolve: { conditions: ['workerd', 'worker', 'module', 'import', 'default'], externalConditions: ['workerd', 'worker'] }, noExternal: true }` — verified in build-C.log, the rollup "not exported" warning disappears and loader/action errors are captured. Exact change (two parts, both required):
1. build the server entry with build-time channel injection instead of the runtime hook:
   `import { sentryOrchestrionPlugin } from '@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild'` in an esbuild build of `server.mjs` (bundle: true, platform node, format esm, external `['@sentry/*','mysql2','react','react-dom','react-dom/server']`, banner `import { createRequire as __sentryCreateRequire } from 'node:module'; const require = __sentryCreateRequire(import.meta.url);`).
   The banner is mandatory: without it the bundle dies at boot with `Error: Dynamic require of "@sentry/server-utils" is not supported` (runC.log), because the injected snippet inside transformed CJS files uses `require` and esbuild's ESM output has none.
2. `Sentry.init({ ..., enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false })`, which stops `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` from registering `Module.registerHooks` — the hook is what makes Deno reject mysql2's `require('../package.json')` (K3).

Evidence, all from my own sink at 127.0.0.1:46311.

A) dist-lazy bundle (mysql2 loaded via `await import('mysql2/promise')` AFTER init), injection OFF, static — runH-injectOFF.log:
{"type":"transaction","name":"GET db","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.remix","spans":["function LOADER root","function LOADER routes/db","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]}
{"type":"transaction","name":"GET users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["function LOADER root","function LOADER routes/users.$id"]}
{"type":"event","exception":"Error: probe-loader-boom-7","mechanism":"auto.function.remix.server","handled":false,"transaction":"GET /boom/7"}
This is the strongest form: the driver genuinely loads after `Sentry.init()`, so the ordering rule the other agent reported is gone, not hidden.

B) Same bundle shape with a module-scope pool (dist-server2), stream lifecycle — runE.log:
{"type":"span","items":["function LOADER root","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users","function LOADER routes/db","http.server GET db"],"raw":[{"name":"mysql2.pool.connect","origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel"},...]}
Static variant (runD.log) gives the same `GET db` transaction with the three db children.

C) Why the hook, not the order, is the defect — dist-lazy bundle with injection ON (default init), runG-injectON.log:
[Sentry] `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` was bundled into your application, so mysql2 ... (false positive; it is external here)
SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'
    at Object.compileFunction (ext:core/01_core.js:1106:31)
    at Object.<anonymous> (.../node_modules/mysql2/lib/connection_config.js:13:21)

D) The obvious one-line "fix" does NOT work on its own — unbundled `server.mjs` + `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false` (runB.log, runI-unbundled-off-stream.log): the process boots, but the sink receives ZERO transactions and ZERO spans, only events. Debug shows `Http.Server Handling incoming request` and no `[Tracing] Starting sampled root span`. Root cause read in the worktree: `packages/remix/src/server/integrations/http.ts:14` sets `disableIncomingRequestSpans: true`, so on Remix the whole server span tree (and with it every db child) comes from the `@remix-run/server-runtime` orchestrion channels — kill runtime injection without replacing it at build time and you lose all tracing. In that state mysql2 produced no db spans either, in static or stream, which also qualifies the other agent's "no instrumentation path is needed at all" claim for mysql2 3.24.3.

So the hoisting is not a recipe.

Works identically as a `bun --preload pin.mjs .output/server/index.mjs` file if you cannot touch the nitro plugin. The proper fix belongs in the SDK: `bindTracingChannelToSpan` must retain the channel it subscribes to (verified to work).
docsImpact: On Bun, database and other library spans need an extra step: Bun garbage-collects `diagnostics_channel` channels that still have subscribers, which silently unsubscribes Sentry's instrumentation, so keep a reference to the channels alive next to your `Sentry.init()` — `import dc from 'node:diagnostics_channel'; globalThis.__sentryPinnedChannels = ['mysql2:query','mysql2:execute','mysql2:connect','mysql2:pool:connect'].map(n => dc.tracingChannel(n));` — after which SolidStart 2's `sentrySolidStart()` vite plugin produces the same `db` spans on Bun as on Node; no Bun-specific build step is required.

The SolidStart guide must say that on SolidStart 2 an uncaught throw inside a file API route (`src/routes/api/*.ts`) or inside a server-rendered page component does not reach Sentry on its own - SolidStart's SSR service builds its own h3 app with no `onError`, so it turns the throw into a 500 before Nitro's error hook (the one `@sentry/nitro` installs) ever sees it - and the guide must show the `createMiddleware([async (event, next) => { try { return await next() } catch (e) { Sentry.captureException(e, { mechanism: { handled: false, type: 'solidstart.middleware' } }); throw e } }, ...])` middleware as the way to capture API-route errors, noting that page render errors still need `withSentryErrorBoundary`. The "Verify" section is currently wrong for SolidStart 2: `~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/index.mdx:452-461` tells the user to confirm the setup with `src/routes/sentry-test.tsx` containing `export async function GET() { throw new Error("Sentry Example API Route Error"); }`, which is exactly the case that produces no error event.

capability: incoming trace (SolidStart 2 + nitro node output on bun 1.4.0, develop SDK 10.67.0)
docsImpact: On Bun, add `bunHttpServerIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` to your `Sentry.init()` in `server/plugins/sentry.ts`: Bun's `node:http` does not emit the `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel the Node SDK relies on, so without it every request shares one process-global trace, incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers are ignored, and no request data is attached; the integration is a no-op under Node, so the same file works for both runtimes.

workaround: Add `@sentry/bun` as a dependency and pass `bunHttpServerIntegration()` in the `integrations` array of the `Sentry.init()` call in `server/plugins/sentry.ts`. It patches `http.Server.prototype.emit` to hand each nitro node:http server to the same core request instrumentation the Node SDK gets from the `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel that bun does not publish, which restores the per-request isolation scope and per-request trace. Use `bunHttpServerIntegration({ spans: false })` if you want to keep only nitro's own h3/srvx spans instead of also getting the core `http.server` span (node emits that span too, so the default is the parity choice). The integration no-ops on node (`process.versions.bun` guard), so a single build runs on both runtimes.
docsImpact: On Bun, add `bunHttpServerIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` to the `integrations` array of the `Sentry.init()` call in your nitro plugin: Bun does not emit the `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel the Node SDK relies on, so without it every request shares one isolation scope and one trace id, and tags set on one request leak into the next. The integration does nothing when the same build runs on Node.

[fetchIntegration()] : []` to Sentry.init (install @sentry/bun alongside @sentry/solidstart). On SolidStart 2, server transactions are named after the request URL (`GET /users/456`, `source: "url"`), not the route pattern, because SolidStart mounts its router as a single Nitro catch-all (`/**`) and the SDK only parameterizes real Nitro routes; this is the same on Bun and on Node, and under the default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` the server span name degrades further to just the method (`GET`), so if you need grouped route names, rename the root span yourself from the Router root for pages (`useCurrentMatches().at(-1)?.route.pattern`) and from each `src/routes/api/**` handler, using `getRootSpan(getActiveSpan()).updateName('GET /users/:id')` plus `http.route` and `sentry.segment.name.source: 'route'`.

details:
REFUTED. A thrown route-handler error does become a Sentry event on SolidStart 1.3 + Cloudflare Workers. The missing piece is not a SolidStart hook, it is a **Nitro plugin registering the h3 `error` hook** — the same hook `@sentry/nitro` (packages/nitro/src/runtime/plugins/server.ts:7) and `@sentry/nuxt` (sentry-cloudflare.server.ts:128) register. SolidStart forwards `server.plugins` in `app.config.ts` straight to Nitro, so the hook is available on workerd; the previous probe simply did not register one.

Probe dir: $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-solidstart-cf-errors (node_modules removed; `npm install` restores it). Files: app.config.ts, src/server-plugin.ts (= RECIPE-nitro-error-plugin.ts), worker.mjs, wrangler.jsonc, src/routes/api/{boom,trace,sentinel}.ts, src/routes/ssrboom.tsx, sinkraw.mjs, raw-final.jsonl, wr-b.log.

Rerun: `npm install` ; `PORT=47311 node $S/qs/sink.mjs > sink-b.log 2>&1 &` ; `npx vinxi build` ; `npx wrangler dev --config wrangler.jsonc --port 47312 --inspector-port 0` ; `curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:47312/api/boom`.

CONTROL (identical build, only `plugins: ['./src/server-plugin.ts']` removed from app.config.ts) — `GET /api/boom` 500, no event, exactly as reported:
  /api/boom=500
  CONTROL span {"items":[{"name":"GET", ... "status":"e...   <- only the errored server span
  CONTROL event [('trace-probe','generic',True)]            <- manual capture still works
  CONTROL event [('sentinel','generic',True)]

WITH the plugin (traceLifecycle 'static', sink /__items, request/user trimmed):
  {"type": "event", "exception": "Error: solidstart-cf boom", "mechanism": "chained", "handled": true, "sdk": "sentry.javascript.cloudflare", "trace_id": "92b8ab0e54a34586bea8489731033862"}
  {"type": "transaction", "name": "GET /api/boom", "op": "http.server", "source": "url", "status": "internal_error", "trace_id": "92b8ab0e54a34586bea8489731033862", "spans": []}
(the compact sink prints `exception.values[0]`, which is the H3 error's `cause`. The raw envelope, raw-final.jsonl, shows the top-level mechanism is the unhandled one:)
  Error | solidstart-cf boom | {"handled": true, "type": "chained", "source": "cause", "exception_id": 1, "parent_id": 0}
  Error | solidstart-cf boom | {"type": "auto.function.nitro.captureErrorHook", "handled": false, "exception_id": 0}
  contexts.nitro: {"method": "GET", "path": "/api/boom"}
The event shares the request's trace_id with the transaction, carries request URL/headers/user.ip_address, and wrangler logs `Sentry Logger [log]: Captured error event \`solidstart-cf boom\`` right before the `[request error] [unhandled]` line.

Also verified: works identically on the develop default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` (event + `span` envelope, trace d1bda53e…); the 3xx/4xx guard in the plugin mirrors the SDK's own `captureErrorHook`; `@sentry/cloudflare` must stay in `rollupConfig.external` or the plugin gets a second module instance.

RESIDUAL GAP (new, not in the original report): an error thrown while Solid renders a *page* (src/routes/ssrboom.tsx) still produces no event — only `{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /ssrboom","status":"internal_error"}`. SolidStart's cloudflare path does `renderToStream(...)` then `stream.pipeTo(writable); return readable`, so the render error surfaces inside the detached pipe after the Response was returned; neither Nitro's `error` hook nor `withSentry` ever sees it. Two dead ends tried: `createHandler(fn, { onError })` — solid's `onError` is the seroval *serializer* callback, never fired for render errors; `mode: 'sync'` — swallows the error entirely and returns 200 with partial HTML, which is worse. API routes, server functions and anything else that throws into h3 are covered by the hook.
docsImpact: The SolidStart guide (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/ has no Cloudflare page at all) needs a "SolidStart on Cloudflare Workers" section stating: use `@sentry/cloudflare` on the server (`@sentry/solidstart`'s server entry is Node-only), wrap the Nitro output with `Sentry.withSentry` in a hand-written `worker.mjs`, keep `@sentry/cloudflare` in `server.rollupConfig.external`, and — this is the part that is otherwise silently missing — register a Nitro plugin via `server.plugins` that does `nitroApp.hooks.hook('error', error => Sentry.captureException(error, { mechanism: { handled: false, type: 'auto.function.nitro.captureErrorHook' } }))`, because without it Nitro swallows every error thrown from a route handler and Sentry only records a 500 transaction; note that errors thrown while a page renders on the server are still not captured, since SolidStart streams the render through a detached pipe.

A SolidStart guide page for Cloudflare Workers needs to say: "@sentry/solidstart's server SDK does not run on Cloudflare Workers; wrap the Nitro output with Sentry.withSentry from @sentry/cloudflare (keeping @sentry/cloudflare in server.rollupConfig.external) and use @sentry/solid for the browser. @sentry/cloudflare has no knowledge of the SolidStart router, so server transactions are named after the raw URL ('GET /api/users/42', source url) with traceLifecycle 'static' and after the method alone ('GET') with span streaming; to get '/api/users/:id' you must add a SolidStart middleware that looks the request path up in the vinxi/routes file-route table and calls span.updateName() plus setAttribute('sentry.segment.name.source', 'route') on the root span."

The SolidStart guide's tracing verification snippet (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/index.mdx:452-460) tells the user to create `export async function GET() { throw new Error("Sentry Example API Route Error"); }` and says clicking the button triggers "an error in the API route" - on SolidStart 2 that error is never sent, so the page needs a correction such as: "On SolidStart 2, errors thrown from an API route handler are caught by SolidStart's internal h3 app and are not captured automatically. To report them, add a try/catch middleware as the first entry of `createMiddleware`'s array form in `src/middleware.ts` that calls `Sentry.captureException(error)` and rethrows; only `'use server'` actions wrapped in `withServerActionInstrumentation` are captured out of the box." The middleware section at index.mdx:196-235 currently documents only `sentryBeforeResponseMiddleware` (trace meta tags) and should carry the same snippet, noting that the object form of `createMiddleware` cannot wrap the handler.

docsImpact: On SolidStart 2 (Nitro 3) the SDK cannot parameterize server transaction names on its own: SolidStart mounts a single `/**` catch-all in Nitro and routes internally, so both API routes and SSR page routes are reported with the raw path (`GET /api/users/42`, `transaction_info.source: "url"`; under span streaming the segment span is named `GET` with `sentry.segment.name.source: "url"`). To get `GET /api/users/:id`, call `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute(pattern)` from `@sentry/server-utils` — for API routes from a global `createMiddleware({ onBeforeResponse })` that rebuilds the pattern from `event.params`, and for page routes from your Router root component during SSR using `useCurrentMatches()`. Routes defined as real Nitro server routes (under `server/` with `nitro({ serverDir })`) are parameterized automatically and need none of this.

capability: db spans (mysql2) in SvelteKit 2.70 + @sentry/sveltekit 10.67.0 (develop) on bun 1.4.0, adapter-node output
details:
Reproduced the reported failure, then made db spans appear on bun with a one-line app change. The reported diagnosis (missed `waitForTracingChannelBinding` retry window) is WRONG: the SDK does subscribe, and then bun garbage-collects the subscription.

Probe dir: $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-sveltekit-bun-dbspans (app/ = SvelteKit app, micro/ = no-framework isolators, RERUN.md = exact commands). Sink: `PORT=41777 node $S/qs/sink.mjs`. Build/run: `cd app && npx vite build && PORT=<port> SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:41777/ bun build/index.js`, drive with `curl /api/db`.

A/B on ONE build config (default traceLifecycle 'stream'), only `app/src/instrumentation.server.ts` differs.

A. Documented wiring (Sentry.init only) — BROKEN, matches the report:
  curl /api/db -> {"rows":[{"id":1,"name":"ada"},{"id":2,"name":"linus"}],"subs":false}
  {"type":"span","items":["function sveltekit.resolve","http.server GET /api/db"]}

B. Same file with `import 'mysql2/promise';` added (position in the file is irrelevant — the import evaluates before the `Sentry.init()` call either way) — WORKS:
  curl /api/db -> {...,"subs":true}
  {"type":"span","items":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users","function sveltekit.resolve","http.server GET /api/db"]}
  With traceLifecycle:'static' the same change gives:
  {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/db","op":"http.server","source":"route","spans":["function sveltekit.resolve","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT * FROM users"]}

Root cause (isolated without SvelteKit, Vite or any bundler, in micro/ with plain `@sentry/node` + mysql2 3.24.3 under `bun app.mjs`):
  bun: "after init, mysql2:query hasSubscribers = true" then "at query time, mysql2:query hasSubscribers = false" -> only ["test probe-root"] in the sink.
  node (same file): true / true -> ["db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users","test probe-root"].
  The SDK debug log on bun shows the subscription DID happen: "Sentry Logger [log]: [instrumentation:mysql2] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly" / "[instrumentation:mysql2] subscribing to channels". So the async-context binding was present at init; nothing was missed.
  micro/dc-gc.mjs (pure runtime test, no Sentry): subscribe to `dc.tracingChannel('probe:chan')` without retaining the object -> bun "immediately: true", "after gc: false"; node "after gc: true". Retaining the channel object keeps the subscribers alive on bun (dc-gc2.mjs). i.e. bun holds diagnostics_channel channels weakly and drops their subscribers once the channel object is unreachable; Node keeps a subscribed channel alive.
  Sequence in the failing case: Sentry subscribes to `mysql2:query`/`:execute`/`:connect`/`:pool:connect` at `Sentry.init()`, before mysql2 is loaded, and keeps no reference to those channels (`subscribeMysql2DiagnosticChannels` in packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql2/mysql2-dc-subscriber.ts subscribes and drops the wrapper). bun collects them; mysql2 then loads and creates fresh, subscriber-less channels of the same names. Loading mysql2 first (or pinning the channels) keeps the object alive so Sentry's subscription survives — that is exactly why the workaround works, and why plain bundled Bun apps where the driver is already in the graph do get db spans.
  This is not mysql2-specific: every diagnostics-channel integration that subscribes at `init()` before its module loads is exposed on bun.

Three fixes verified on bun (micro/app-b.mjs, app-c.mjs, app-d.mjs — all produce ["db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users", ...]):
  - `import 'mysql2/promise'` in the same file as `Sentry.init()` (before or after the Sentry import),
  - creating the pool in that file,
  - user-side pinning: `globalThis.__keep = ['mysql2:query','mysql2:execute','mysql2:connect','mysql2:pool:connect'].map(n => require('node:diagnostics_channel').tracingChannel(n))`.
SDK-side fix (not applied, repo untouched): retain a module-level strong reference to every channel the SDK subscribes to.

Two setup facts from the original report reproduce and still hold: the Vite plugin is `@sentry/sveltekit/vite` on develop, and `experimental.instrumentation.server: true` + `src/instrumentation.server.ts` is required or no span/transaction envelopes are emitted at all.

Processes started (sink 41777, bun servers on 43117/52341/52987/53829) were all killed; micro/node_modules removed.
workaround: In `src/instrumentation.server.ts`, import the database driver in the same file as `Sentry.init()` — `import 'mysql2/promise';` next to `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/sveltekit';` (order within the file does not matter). That keeps the `mysql2:*` diagnostics channels reachable so bun cannot garbage-collect Sentry's subscription before mysql2 loads. Creating the pool in that file works equally well. Generic form for any channel-based integration on bun: hold a strong reference to the channels, e.g. `globalThis.__sentryKeepChannels = ['mysql2:query','mysql2:execute','mysql2:connect','mysql2:pool:connect'].map(n => tracingChannel(n))` from `node:diagnostics_channel`.
docsImpact: On Bun, import your database driver (or create the connection/pool) inside `src/instrumentation.server.ts`, in the same file as `Sentry.init()` — Bun drops `node:diagnostics_channel` subscriptions whose channel object is unreachable, so a driver that first loads after `Sentry.init()` publishes to fresh, unsubscribed channels and produces no `db` spans.

details:
REFUTED. The reported symptom reproduces exactly, but it is a missing-integration problem with a one-line fix, not a bun limitation.

## Setup (all under $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-sveltekit-bun-outgoingfetch/)

`npx sv@latest create --template minimal --types ts --no-add-ons --no-install app` -> SvelteKit ^2.63.0, svelte ^5.56.1, vite ^8.0.16 (same shape the reporter used: no `svelte.config.js`, kit config inside the `sveltekit()` Vite plugin). Then `npm install @sveltejs/adapter-node` and the develop tarball set on one line:

```
npm install $S/pack/sentry-sveltekit-10.67.0.tgz $S/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $S/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz \
  $S/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $S/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz \
  $S/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz $S/pack/sentry-browser-10.67.0.tgz $S/pack/sentry-svelte-10.67.0.tgz \
  $S/pack/sentry-cloudflare-10.67.0.tgz $S/pack/sentry-bundler-plugins-10.67.0.tgz $S/pack/sentry-browser-utils-10.67.0.tgz \
  $S/pack/sentry-replay-10.67.0.tgz $S/pack/sentry-replay-canvas-10.67.0.tgz $S/pack/sentry-feedback-10.67.0.tgz \
  $S/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz
```

(I confirm the reporter's packing note: `@sentry/browser-utils`, `@sentry/replay` (packages/replay-internal), `@sentry/replay-canvas`, `@sentry/feedback` were not in `$S/pack` and had to be `npm pack`ed from the worktree. I added them to `$S/pack` for later agents. `@sentry/bundler-plugins` WAS already there.)

Wiring is the reporter's: `sentrySvelteKit({ autoUploadSourceMaps: false, adapter: 'node' })` from `@sentry/sveltekit/vite` before `sveltekit({ adapter: adapter(), experimental: { instrumentation: { server: true }, tracing: { server: true } } })`; `src/instrumentation.server.ts` calls `Sentry.init`; `src/hooks.server.ts` exports `sentryHandle()`/`handleErrorWithSentry()`. Route `src/routes/api/out/+server.ts` does a bare global `await fetch(`${process.env.REC_URL}/__rec/from-sveltekit`)`. Sink at `sink.mjs` (copy of `$S/qs/sink.mjs` plus a `/__rec/` header recorder readable at `/__recs`), port 47611. Build: `npx vite build`. Run: `PORT=<port> SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:47611/ REC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:47611 bun build/index.js`. Driven with `curl` from outside the app process, sentinel = `Sentry.captureMessage('sentinel')` on `/api/hello`.

## 1. Baseline on bun 1.4.0 — symptom reproduced (app-bun-baseline.log)

```
{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/out","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"b3ee296ec7544f148a5e66727f6e063c","sdk":"sentry.javascript.sveltekit","spans":["function sveltekit.resolve"],"hasRequestData":false}
--- recs ---
[{"url":"/__rec/from-sveltekit","sentry-trace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null}]
```

## 2. node v26.5.0 control, identical `build/` (app-node-control.log)

```
{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/out",...,"trace_id":"29a371b67451408593e59e79a3d660d1",...,"spans":["function sveltekit.resolve","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:47611/__rec/from-sveltekit"]}
--- recs ---
{"url":"/__rec/from-sveltekit","sentry-trace":"29a371b67451408593e59e79a3d660d1-94ff6be37a904a0d-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=29a371b67451408593e59e79a3d660d1,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Fout,sentry-sampled=true,...","traceparent":null}
```

So the reporter's claim and root cause (`@sentry/node`'s NodeFetch integration is undici-diagnostics-channel-based, and bun does not emit `undici:request:create`) are both correct as stated.

## 3. The fix: add `fetchIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun`

`@sentry/bun` ships its own fetch integration that does not touch diagnostics_channel — it patches global `fetch` via `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` from `@sentry/core` (worktree `packages/bun/src/integrations/fetch.ts`, exported at `packages/bun/src/index.ts:209`). `@sentry/sveltekit` on the server is `@sentry/node`, so it never gets that integration, but nothing stops you adding it.

`src/instrumentation.server.ts`:
```ts
import { fetchIntegration } from '@sentry/bun';
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/sveltekit';

const isBun = typeof globalThis.Bun !== 'undefined';

Sentry.init({
  dsn: '...',
  tracesSampleRate: 1.0,
  tunnel: process.env.SENTRY_TUNNEL,
  integrations: isBun ? [fetchIntegration()] : [],
});
```

bun, `traceLifecycle: 'static'` (app-bun-gated.log):
```
{"t":"transaction","name":"GET /api/out","spans":["function sveltekit.resolve","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:47611/__rec/from-sveltekit"],"trace":"338f9934865349a78662bc3b8cdb2946"}
--- recs (last) ---
{"url":"/__rec/from-sveltekit","sentry-trace":"338f9934865349a78662bc3b8cdb2946-862e814c4e19d21f-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=338f9934865349a78662bc3b8cdb2946,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Fout,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rate=1","traceparent":null}
```
The client span's parent trace id matches the server transaction's, and the recorder now sees both headers.

bun, default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` (app-bun-fetchintegration-stream.log) — also works, span name is the low-cardinality form:
```
{"t":"span","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","function sveltekit.resolve","http.server GET /api/out"]}
```

## 4. Why the `isBun` gate is required

Without the gate, the same build on node emits the span TWICE (bun's `fetchIntegration` and node's undici NodeFetch integration both fire) — app-node-fetchintegration.log:
```
{"t":"transaction","name":"GET /api/out","spans":["function sveltekit.resolve","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:47611/__rec/from-sveltekit","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:47611/__rec/from-sveltekit"]}
```
So the integration must be added conditionally, or the app must be bun-only.

## Notes and confirmations of the reporter's other observations

- `@sentry/sveltekit/vite` (not `@sentry/sveltekit`) is where `sentrySvelteKit` lives on develop; the repo's own e2e app agrees (`dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/sveltekit-2-kit-tracing/vite.config.ts` imports from `@sentry/sveltekit/vite`).

  import require$$0 from "@sentry/core";
  SyntaxError: The requested module '@sentry/core' does not provide an export named 'default'
      at async analyse (.../node_modules/@sveltejs/kit/src/core/postbuild/analyse.js:106:62)
The head of that chunk shows the whole family: `import require$$0$1 from "@sentry/conventions/attributes"`, `import require$$0$3 from "@opentelemetry/api"`, `import require$$4 from "@sentry/core/server"`.

ROOT CAUSE (verified, not theorised). `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` (packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/bundler/vite.ts, `config()`) force-bundles the instrumented module plus `@sentry/server-utils`, but NOT `@sentry/core`, `@sentry/conventions` or `@opentelemetry/api`. The snippet injected into CJS `mysql` `require()`s `@sentry/server-utils`; under a hoisted layout that bare specifier resolves normally and vite picks server-utils' **CJS** build, whose `require('@sentry/core')` rollup-commonjs rewrites into a default import of an external named-exports-only ESM package. Under pnpm the bare specifier does not resolve from mysql's isolated location, so the plugin's own `resolveId` fallback (`resolveOrchestrionRuntimeRequest`) resolves the ESM build and the CJS path is never taken. That is why `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` apps (dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/cloudflare-orchestrion-mysql) never see it: the Workers build bundles everything.

Variants I tried on the npm app (all in appD, `npx vite build -c <config>`):
- vite.config.js (docs shape)                                   -> FAIL, error above
- vite.config.a.js  ssr.noExternal ['@sentry/core']              -> FAIL, same error moves to '@sentry/conventions/attributes'
- vite.config.b.js  ssr.noExternal [/^@sentry\//,'@opentelemetry/api'] -> builds, but HARMFUL: it bundles `@sentry/sveltekit` itself and the Node SDK boots instead of the Cloudflare one. Sink shows `"sdk":"sentry.javascript.sveltekit","runtime":"node"`, the `http.server GET /db-mysql` child span disappears (`"spans":["db SELECT * FROM users"]`) and the worker logs `[Sentry] Failed to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks`. Do not document the regex.
- vite.config.c.js  ssr.noExternal ['@sentry/core','@sentry/conventions','@opentelemetry/api'] -> builds AND correct at runtime: `"sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","spans":["http.server GET /db-mysql","db SELECT * FROM users"]`
- vite.config.d.js  sentrySvelteKit({ buildTimeInstrumentation: false }) -> builds, but no transform, so no db spans.

Do not use a `/^@sentry\//` regex: it force-bundles `@sentry/sveltekit` and boots the Node SDK instead of the Cloudflare one. details:
REFUTED. SvelteKit 2 + adapter-node on Deno 2.9.0 with @sentry/sveltekit 10.67.0 (develop) does emit `db` spans, in both trace lifecycles. The report's two claims come apart: the mysql2 500 is real, but it is a Deno bug (denoland/deno#36240), not the absence of db instrumentation, and it does not affect the `mysql` driver at all.

Probe dir: $SCRATCH/deep/verify4-M-sveltekit-deno-dbspans/
  app/                     SvelteKit 2.70 + adapter-node 5.5 + svelte 5 + vite 6, wiring identical to the report (sentrySvelteKit from '@sentry/sveltekit/vite', mysql/mysql2 + @sentry/* external, Sentry.init at the top of src/hooks.server.js, sentryHandle + handleErrorWithSentry)
  app/src/lib/db.js        module-scope `mysql2/promise` connection      -> route /db
  app/src/routes/db2/+server.js  `mysql` v2 connection inside the handler -> route /db2
  app/prewarm-json.mjs     the one-line workaround, used via `deno run --preload`
  jsontest/t.mjs           minimal repro: registerHooks pass-through + require('*.json')
  runD.log (no workaround, stream), runE.log (workaround, stream), runF.log (workaround, static), runG.log (--preload workaround, stream), runA.log/runB.log (earlier runs, same conclusions)

1) The `mysql` driver needs NO change whatsoever. Unmodified reported setup, `LIFECYCLE=stream`, sink on 41777:
   ping -> pong [200]
   db  -> {"message":"Internal Error"} [500]
   db2 -> {"driver":"mysql","rows":2} [200]
   sink:
     span  ['http.server GET /ping']
     span  ['db SELECT users', 'http.server GET /db2']
     span  ['http.server GET /sentinel']
   raw: {"name": "SELECT users", "status": "ok", "parent_span_id": "...", "origin": "auto.db.mysql"}
   So "no db span" is wrong even in the exact configuration the report ran.

2) mysql2 works too once Deno's JSON bug is sidestepped. Warm mysql2's package.json into the CJS require cache before Sentry registers its hooks. Two equivalent forms, both verified:
   a) run flag only, no app code change (runG):
      HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=41784 deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-ffi \
        --preload ./prewarm-json.mjs build/index.js
      where prewarm-json.mjs is:  import { createRequire } from 'node:module'; createRequire(import.meta.url)('mysql2/package.json');
   b) the same two lines at the very top of src/hooks.server.js, above the `Sentry.init` import.
   Result (stream, runG):  db -> {"driver":"mysql2","rows":2} [200]
     span ['db SELECT users', 'http.server GET /db']
     span ['db SELECT users', 'http.server GET /db2']
   raw origin for /db: "auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel"  <- the SDK's channel injection really did instrument mysql2 on Deno
   Result (static, runF): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["db SELECT id, name FROM users"]}
                          {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db2",...,"spans":["db SELECT id, name FROM users"]}

3) The crash is Deno's, not the SDK's. jsontest/t.mjs registers a pass-through `Module.registerHooks({resolve,load})` with no Sentry anywhere:
   -- deno 2.9.0 no hook:            json ok: {"a":1}
   -- deno 2.9.0 with pass-through hook: json FAIL: SyntaxError Unexpected token ':'
   -- node 26 with hook:             json ok: {"a":1}
   Any library that `require()`s a .json at runtime breaks under Deno the moment anything registers sync module hooks. mysql2 does that at connection_config.js:13; `mysql` v2 does not, which is the whole difference between /db and /db2.

Two secondary observations that stand independent of the verdict:
- `[instrumentation] failed to inject diagnostics-channel into mysql2: TypeError: transform is not a function` is printed on every run, together with the always-on "`@sentry/server-runtime-injection` was bundled into your application" warning, yet the package is NOT bundled (the stack points at app/node_modules/@sentry/server-runtime-injection/build/esm/vendored/...) and mysql2 IS instrumented (origin auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel). One mysql2 file fails to transform under Deno while the ones that matter succeed, so the always-on warning is a false alarm here and sends users down the wrong path.
- `[Sentry] Runtime hook registered, injected libraries=[]` is logged before any library loads, so it never reflects reality.
docsImpact: On Deno, database spans work for SvelteKit adapter-node builds (verified for `mysql` and `mysql2`), but a Deno bug (denoland/deno#36240) makes `require()` of a JSON file fail once the SDK installs its module hooks, so drivers that read their own package.json at runtime — mysql2 among them — throw `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` on first use; load that JSON into the require cache before the SDK initializes, with a `--preload` file (or two lines at the top of `src/hooks.server.js`) containing `createRequire(import.meta.url)('mysql2/package.json')`, and note that the `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` "was bundled into your application" warning can fire spuriously on Deno even when instrumentation is working.

workaround: Either (a) one line, using shipped SDK code: `import { fetchIntegration } from '@sentry/cloudflare';` and `Sentry.init({ ..., integrations: [fetchIntegration()] })` in hooks.server.js — verified to produce the `http.client` span and both `sentry-trace` and `baggage` headers under both trace lifecycles, including for SvelteKit's `event.fetch`; or (b) copy the WinterCG fetch patcher into the app as a userland integration from `@sentry/core` primitives (`addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest` + `isSentryRequestUrl` + `shouldPropagateTraceForUrl`), see src/userland-fetch-integration.js in the probe dir. Both are ~equally effective; (a) drags @sentry/cloudflare into a Deno server dependency tree, (b) keeps the dependency list clean. The pre-existing escape hatch of switching the call to `node:http` also works but changes application code. The real fix belongs in the SDK: `@sentry/node` (or `@sentry/deno`) should ship a global-fetch integration and enable it when the undici diagnostics channels are absent, which is exactly the Deno case.
docsImpact: On Deno, outgoing requests made with the global `fetch()` (including SvelteKit's `event.fetch`) get no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, because Sentry's Node fetch instrumentation listens on undici's `diagnostics_channel` events and Deno's `fetch` is native rather than undici; until the SDK ships a global-fetch integration for this runtime, either add `fetchIntegration()` from `@sentry/cloudflare` to `integrations`, or make the call through `node:http`/`node:https`, which is instrumented and propagates trace headers correctly.

No `getVariableForExportName`, no `"default" is not exported by @sentry/conventions/dist/attributes.mjs`. The build-time channel injection is in the output: `grep -c orchestrion:mysql:query app/.output/server/chunks/build/router-CkZFiwOD.mjs` -> 2. What made it work is the dependency set, not the framework: install the whole develop tarball set as overrides (@sentry/{tanstackstart-react,react,browser,node,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry,bundler-plugins,browser-utils,feedback,replay,replay-canvas}) — see app/package.json `pnpm.overrides`. 2) ROOT CAUSE OF THE MISSING DB SPANS IS BUN GC, NOT INJECTION. Bun 1.4.0 drops diagnostics_channel subscribers as soon as the channel object is collected; the SDK subscribes as `diagnosticsChannel.tracingChannel(NAME).subscribe(...)` and keeps no reference (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql.ts and every other channel integration; the Bun/Deno eager branch is packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/instrumentation.ts:100). Same signal in-app (prior run-bun-obs.log): "[obs] after init: [ true, true, true, true, true ]" then "[obs] t+6s: [ false, false, false, false, false ]".

3) BEFORE/AFTER ON THE SAME FRESH BUILD (traceLifecycle stream, default; sink on 41733, app on 41732, driven by curl).
Control, exactly the documented file, `bun --preload ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs` (v2-final-control.log, 0 `op: db` lines):

Fixed, same file plus three retained channels (v2-final-fixed.log, 4 `op: db` lines):
  [{"type":"span","trace_id":"c0b4010f5e1f481db289e5588c24bb7e","items":["middleware globalRequestMiddleware","db SELECT","db SELECT users"],"raw":[{"name":"globalRequestMiddleware","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.middleware.tanstackstart"},{"name":"SELECT","parent_span_id":"a3415e4d3b0f19ce","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.db.mysql"},{"name":"SELECT users","parent_span_id":"a3415e4d3b0f19ce","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.db.mysql"}]}, {... second request identical ...}]
`traceLifecycle: 'static'` also records them (v2-run-bun-fixed-static.log) but each db span arrives as its OWN transaction envelope ({"type":"transaction","name":"SELECT 1 + 1 AS solution","op":"db","parent_span_id":...}) because the `middleware globalRequestMiddleware` root finishes before the queries do — stream is the better shape here. Unrelated to db spans, bun still has no `http.server` root span for the nitro node-server (node run of the same build has one: run-node-stream.log "root description: GET /api/db-mysql"); on bun the segment is the request middleware span.

Root cause, read from the source: packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/index.ts calls `instrumentUndici()`, and packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/undici-instrumentation.ts is a vendored @opentelemetry/instrumentation-undici that only subscribes to the `undici:request:*` diagnostics channels. Deno's `fetch` is the native Rust implementation and never publishes those channels, so nothing fires. No init option, entry shape, trace lifecycle or Deno flag can change that — there is no other hook point in the node SDK for the global `fetch`.

REFUTED PARTIALLY by a userland integration (not shipped, not documented): re-implementing @sentry/cloudflare's `fetchIntegration` on top of primitives @sentry/core already exports (`addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest`, which patch `globalThis.fetch`) restores both the span and the headers on Deno. Files: .output/server/deno-fetch-integration.mjs, .output/server/instrument.fetchfix.mjs, .output/server/deno-entry-fetchfix.mjs.

    recorder: {"url":"/rec","sentryTrace":"f8e0a54e7ea44c5280007ab146b580e2-b591d3b9aa05a293-1","baggage":"...sentry-trace_id=f8e0a54e7ea44c5280007ab146b580e2,sentry-sampled=true..."}

The client span is correctly parented under the server segment and carries the same trace id, so the OTel context propagation into `startInactiveSpan` works on Deno; only the channel-based trigger is missing.

TanStack Start is not implicated anywhere: the framework's own request/function middleware spans and route handling behave the same on both runtimes.

Rerun: `cd <probe>/.output/server && PORT=43121 RECORDER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:43119/rec deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-ffi deno-entry.mjs` (broken) vs `... deno-entry-fetchfix.mjs` (works), with `PORT=43117 node ../../sink.mjs` and `PORT=43119 node ../../recorder.mjs` running.
docsImpact: The TanStack Start guide has no Deno page at all (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/tanstackstart-react/ contains no mention of "deno"); if one is added it must say: on Deno the server SDK does not instrument outgoing `fetch()` — no `http.client` span is created and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers are attached — because the instrumentation listens on undici's `diagnostics_channel` events, which Deno's native fetch does not emit; use `node:http`/`node:https` or wrap the call in `Sentry.startSpan()` until the SDK ships a global-fetch fallback.

workaround: Add `noExternals: ['@sentry/tanstackstart-react']` to the `nitro()` Vite plugin options: `nitro({ noExternals: ['@sentry/tanstackstart-react'] })`. Nitro then bundles the SDK into the server output instead of leaving it a bare import, so `sentryTanstackStart()`'s route-pattern plugin can substitute `__SENTRY_ROUTE_PATTERNS__` inside `wrapFetchWithSentry`. Verify it landed with `grep -l 'users/\$userId' .output/server/_libs/sentry__tanstackstart-react.mjs` before deploying. Also use vite 8.x; vite 7.3.2 with nitro 3.0.260903-beta crashes rollup during the server build regardless of Sentry.
docsImpact: In the TanStack Start guide (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/tanstackstart-react/manual-setup/index.mdx and features/sentryTanstackStart.mdx, neither of which mentions nitro externals today), the vite.config example must read `nitro({ noExternals: ['@sentry/tanstackstart-react'] })` with the note: "Nitro must bundle `@sentry/tanstackstart-react` into the server output. If it is left as an external dependency, the Sentry Vite plugin cannot inject your route patterns and server transactions will be named by raw URL (`GET /users/123`) instead of by route (`GET /users/$userId`); no warning is emitted, so confirm with `grep '\$' .output/server/_libs/sentry__tanstackstart-react.mjs` after building." Add that running the nitro `node` output under Deno needs no Sentry-specific change beyond a two-line entry (`import './instrument.server.mjs'; import './index.mjs';`) next to `index.mjs`, since Deno has no `node --import`.
